clubs.name: Across the Waves FC - Wide Bay

scores.comment: The values detailed in paragraphs and doesn't expressed in a way that can easily remembered (one word phrases). At the same time MCE's core beliefs are very clear and put in practice.

The GCK MVP is well structured and holistic. The only missing component is the a multi-year plan connected to the club's misson and vision. There is a register of success measures of the last four years, but there are no milestones attached to the current planing yet.

The club has a brief but well-structured MVP. Long term focus in football development is clearly articulated through the "Developing Individuals In a team Environment" document, but multi-year linking is somewhat missing in an operational and financial plan. It is evident that such planning happens at Lions FC as they are strong in both area although it would be great to see it connected to the academy area.

LLFC has a very complete structure to articulate their beliefs. The MVP document is well-structured, multi-faceted and refers other key documents - including the newly introduced club-specific STRIKE and SPARK, player and coach development documents.
Clear and conscise with good graphics, references to club's heritage and history. Only the operational, financial link missing with a multi-year lens.

OFC's document covers most aspects of the MVP well. The club philosophy is articulated through a coaching philosophy which is important, but not providing more on overarching beliefs. No multi-year plan is embedded to guide progress.
Great MVP with a holistic approach and success mesaures. It is refreshing to see that Education is a core pillar.

Strong future focus with a 2026 to 2030 strategic plan which includes people and cultrue, financial and facility planning and a consistent MVP and Values framework. The added philsophy and daily behaviours documents are great expansion on the strategy,

Wynnum's startegic pillars are built out with short term (1-2 years) and mid term (3-5 years) stepping stones and targets. The MVP is well-presented with detailed values and behaviours. The club philosphy need to be added to round up the club's "Teamwork"-framework.

While everything is covered in the document, the structure slightly amalgamates certain elements. Aims and Mission, Philsophy and Game Principles are inter-related but having a separate section for each could add more significance to each. The only missing component is the multi-year plan that connects other areas (finance, facilities) to football.

The documentation is very thoughtful and created with metaphores to allow the Hawks to fly: Rise and Sore are constants and referenced in different parts. The multi-year framework is also described from a Technical, Operational and Financial perspective but the breakdown and the span of the plan (1 year, 3-5 years?) is not specified.

Magic's MVP covers all key areas with good detail. A more detailed breakdown of their multi-year plan of 2025-2028 can be suggested. The Focus areas are a great addition for clarity and guidance. The Participation, Community, Programs, Promoting and Education pillars are also strong and display business-minded and service-centred thinking.
Professionally crafted, strategic plan spans from 2024 to 2028.It would be interesting to review what was achieved in the first 2.5 years in all areas.

Good values statements, complex mission and vision description and the philosophy is explained through guiding principles. There is reference to ops and finances but the multi-year stages could be layed out in more detail.
Highlights of the Redlands MVP are the ABC of their Player Identity that complements the values and the 2026-2029 four year plan expanding on five key strategic area.
Very well structured document with multi-year action plans and measurable success indicators.
Well-crafted blueprint for the club, stand out statements about commitment culture and thoughtful five year plan (2026-2030). Definitely a step up compared to the former MVP.
Brief and clear MVP. While it defines operational aspects through the club's organisational structure it is recommended to add multi-year plan for each pillar's execution and a few measurable KPI's.
An improved doucment under new leadership. All areas are covered except a multi-year approach to build their pillars.

The more than 100 pages MVP might be great in detail but lacks some practicality. Separate club and player values are unique and bring 12 values to be upheld. After the declaration of their three philosophy pillars the document proivides more insight. about core football programming that is less relevant to the core of the MVP. Credit to the club management for the 2025-2027 plan. It'd be interesting to track progress for the first 1.5 years with an updated milstones document.

The blueprints spread across three documents and it would be advised to bring them into one holistic presentation. The Startegic Plan attempts to resonate with the Whole of Football (FQ) plans which shows good alignment. The Club Philosophy is somewhat un-clarified, although it is innate in the LTAD framework and the metaphore they use about the growth of a bamboo tree.
One key elements, the club Values and their explanation is missing. All other aspects is covered with a multi-year approach and tracking.
Excellent plan with Short, Medium and Long Term check points spanning to a 2034 for the club in different areas.
The main part of the document is strong and there would not be necesseary to add all football development pages to the MVP. Good reasoning on values and multi-year approach.
Great one page summary from values to club vision and additional documents on Strategic Objectives and football plans. A multi-year approach with stepping stones should be adopted and documented.

Highly detailed document outlining exactly how players are developed at the club through each age & phase. As mentioned in last year's comment, the Coaching Methodology Principles section needs to be built out further.

Document contains good detail around philosophy, LTADF, and technical Age-Specific Guidelines. Training session framework & coaching methodology principles need more detail around how these are implemented according to each age and phase to provide a clearer picture of program delivery

In the first year of a new club development philosophy, the document provides far greater detail around how players are developed at the club. To take this to the next level, more detail around age-specific delivery in terms of technical/tactical content, and coaching methodology is required

There is some good detail around club philosophy and age-specific content, however, absence of a LTADF makes it difficult to get a clear picture of how player development is planned and implemented. More detail around training session framework for each age & phase, and coaching methodology principles is required

Document contains some good detail and is a noticeable improvement on 2025. It is clear the type of player the club wants to develop and the key principles that support it. More detail around the breakdown of age-specific guidelines in terms of key content, and more guidance on how coaches deliver during sessions will provide a well-rounded resource

Document is a little difficult to follow in terms of its flow. Some good detail around the Olympic player, but still a little surface level in terms of age-specific breakdown for technical content & coaching methodology

A good, detailed document that provides a clear picture of player development at the club. More in depth detail into coaching methodolody through different session types & practice components would be valuable. Developing a process for technical execution would be recommended

Document has obviously been re-done since last year and provides an over-arching idea of how players are developed at the club. Really like the idea around the technical toolbox. Some detail missing around age-specific delivery, especially for U14 and above. Strongly suggest that everything is placed into one document

Document provides a surface level overview of player development at the club. Giving some consideration to developing what the 'wolves' player looks like will help guide more detail through age-specific guidelines and technical/tactical content. More detail around how coaches coach during sessions & matchday is required

The 2026 edition of the P2 document for Rochedale has changed positively and provides an effective overview of the player development direction that the club wishes to head in. To add to this, more detail around technical/tactical content by age and phase is required. In addition, a breakdown of how the P-L-A-Y coaching methodology is used through each age and phase would provide a clearer picture. Big task will be in the delivery and implementation of this philosophy
Surface level document with no detail attached to it. Very difficult to get a clear picture of the type of player the club wishes to develop and how they do it through each age & phase

Some small but key additions have been made to this document by the new TD. The inclusion of 1v1 and '120s' shift the focus back onto developing dominant individual players. Given that the ecological dynamics approach is still being used, more detail around how this is implemented in each age & phase is required. This is a difficult approach for the untrained coach.
Only a very surface level overview of player development. More detail is required, especially around age and phase delivery

A surface level overview of player development and requires more detail, especially around age-specific guidelines. The document is wordy - recommend introducing tables/diagrams etc so convey information in a clear way

Document is a good starting point to provide an overview of how players are developed at the club. The next step is to provide further detail on age-sepcific guidelines to provide a clear idea on how players are developed at each age and phase

Document is a good starting point to provide an overview of how players are developed at the club. There is some really good detail around LTADF that needs to be built out into greater detail through age-specific guidelines to get a clear idea around how players are developed in each age and phase. A breakdown of coaching methodology and weekly session structures in each age and phase would also be beneficial
Document lacks key detail in most of the criteria. Highly recommend following the document structure outlined in the P2 workshop

Documents contains a lack of detail, is surface level, and doesn't follow a logical process or structure. Age and phase delivery needs to be built out. All components of the line item should be contained in one document, not separate documents
All information for the line item needs to be included into one document following a logical format. Surface level overview of player development with a lack of age-specific detail

Some good information Contained in the document, but a lack of detail in terms of age-specific breakdown. If using components from Football Queensland documents, this needs to be appropriately referenced as 'supporting FQ Player Develpment Principles'
Document doesn't follow a logical flow or progression with a lack of detail around many of the criteria. Suggest looking back on the P2 workshop
Comment reflects the level of effort put into this document

Document serves as a good starting point and general overview of player development at the club. While having a specific playing style is important, I would advise that this support player development pricniples, not guide it

Document contains a lot of detail about the 'what', but little detail around how players use the 'when' and 'how'  to execute. Consideration the philosophy focuses on decison-making, this is fundamental. More detail on coaching methodology and session framework is required
Document is brief and lacks key detail, which is disappointing considering a development meeting was held with the club specifically around this document. Further detail in all areas in required

For each of the playing principles listed in the key moments there may be more detail per age and stage.  This may be linked to what does success or attainment look like?  What does it look like for an U10 female player to STAY on the ball?  What does it look like for her to MOVE the ball etc.  Having a way of tracking what attainment looks like may help shape discussion around individual player development within the playing style.

There may need to be some thought around aligning the junior PS document with the boys and girls.  There is no real need to have a sepeerate document for gender as long as the key principles of the appracoh are detailed.  There may be consideration about simplifying the playing style docs into higher level process based application.

More detail may be required per age and stage.  Having principles based upon th emain moments needs to be clear for all age group coaches across both genders.  It may be beneficial to have some graphics on how a principle based approach can be applied to junior age groups.

More detail requried about the game day approach fro junior age groups.  What are the key outcomes coaches should be looking for players to action in relation to individual player development at these age groups.

The document itself contains good information however the formatting needs review.  This document needs to be easy for coaches to understand what is required per age and stage.  There is so much AI formatting heavy that it masks the content of what should be a regularly referenced cotent.

There may need to be more information around the coaching detail per area of the game model.  How do coahces correct or change on game day Vs highlighting areas of delivery within training sessions and periodisation.  How much scope is there for a change of focus from the periodisation based upon what players need?

There may need to be more detail around junior development.  There may need to be some consideration as to WHY the club want to deploy a certain playing style?  What are the technical tactical physical psychological outcomes by doing things a certain way?  How does that shape what is brought to life.

There may need to be more detail in the junior areas of what is requried for a game day model.  The document may need to be formatted in a better way so that there is more clarity per age and stage / gender in the key areas of deliverables for coaches.

There may need to be more detail around the junior phases for both genders.  Having more thought about the WHY behind the playing style may be important.  What are the outcomes as per the 4 corner model that are are a result of playing a certain way.

There needs to be more detail about how the principles are applied per age and stage.  What would coaches at each age and stage be looking at delivering in the key moments of the game.  There is no detail around the defenisive blocks or build up sections.  What defensive block do the club like to deploy? Why is that the case?  Can there be more evidence as to why the principles have been applied.  Principle listing is fine but what ones are more important at what ages?

Really like the use of the 'risk register' as a guide for the club to keep playing style on check.  There may need to be more detail about the layering of principles of play per age and stage.  What are the most important concenpts for juniors - to the 11 v 11 game to more senior age groups.  More detail requried around the age and stage delivery.

Nice to have some concepts for GKs within this model framework.  It may be worth having some more detail around the ages and stages and what is most important in each age and stage as a hyrachy of delivery.  Ie for an U9 what is most important principles for Magic when defending - what is this for an u18 and so on.
The document content may be better formatted in a way that can be better udnerstood by all age group coaches.  This may be simplified per age and stage.

There may need to be more detail regarding the breakdown of the style of play per age and stage.  There needs to be some more cosndieration about what the hyrachy of importance is on each of the main moments per age and stage.  For example in defending does N Lakes want to see players win it high or drop off?  When does this change? There may also need to be more detail regarding the detail for each age group in the younger ages that is easy to udnerstand for each age group coach.

Key details are shown regarding the player behavious over playing formations.  When using the inspirational club guide for player behaviours like Liverpool and Atlanta it would be curcial to ensure that this is always linked back to what the club itself want to see at each of the ages and stages.
Good detail - especially within the areas of relationalism for the players and what is important per age an dstage.

May need to be some one pager docs that simplifiy what is required per age and stage.  Their may be some further consideration as to what the coaches should be focusing on as a priority within each age and stage delivery.

There is a lot of slides in this area that go into detail about the specific movements of players - it may be that there needs to be more summary or principles around the requried process.  Age group coaches would struggle to digest all of this information - this needs to be simplified per age and stage.

There may need to be more detail around the junior ages and stages - there is no specific break down for junior age groups and or the principles of play for this delivery.  What is important for the club to see on game day at these ages? Why?
Good detail with the break down of ages and phases - good idea to have some cues that age groop coaches can bring to life the playing style easily by referenicg.
Good detail - there may need to be more informaton given as to whom is responsible for the delivery of these plans.  How doe staff ensure that this indeed is being adhered to and followed.
There may need to be more detail around what objective data is used for quantifying player progressioj.  It is mentioned in the doc but what is it? Who collects it? How do players see it?

There may need to be more detail about which staff do which portion of delivery within the player development process.  Who does what area - by when?  How is the overall process assessed as working well or not?  Is there an annual review?

The club may need to consider how the assessment of players is completed?  What data is collected - how are bias removed from player assessment - is there the ability to record objective data - if so what is used and when?

IDP tracker needs to have more detail as to what is tracked and how.  If asking players to track outcome or objective based assessment they need to have the tools to properly assess this.  There may be greater need to have the document formatted in a way that acts as a working process tool.  Ie what do coaches have to do? why ?  what does this look like for TDs and lead coaches so that they can track if the individual development is being impacted.

Good detail - there may need to be more informaton given as to whom is responsible for the delivery of these plans.  How doe staff ensure that this indeed is being adhered to and followed.  There may be better guidance for coaches HOW to better assess player performance.

There may need to be more consideration as to how this document can be used to assess the coaches ability to develop in line with a documented process.  IE are the caoches doing what they need to for indivdiual development?  There may also need to be greater consideration or guidance for coaches - for when theya re completing player assessments.  How do they arrive at the scores they do.

This document has a good level of detail in terms of listing what is required from the club fro indivdiual development.  The document itsefl may need to include greater "how to" for each area of the individual player philosophy.

The document may need to consider how the contents inform the coaches on what is requried as an overarching approach to individual development.  It needs to give greater structure on what the plan or process is on how to best develop individuals.  Outside of IDPs there needs to be another layer of detail as a working process / policy for the club to gauge how well they plan works and how much they conform to that plan.  Ie how does the club score teh accuracy and content of its IDPs en masse.  How does the club know that the coachea are scoring the 1-5 criteria correctly - what other factors could be used?  Could this be objective data?

There may need to be more though as to how this document acts as a working process at the club or methodology to individual development plans.  It may be that more broader thought is given.  Philosophically how does the club improve an individual.  How can there be greater detail in underatdning exactly what each player needs and when?  Do the club believe that strengths are doubled down on or weaknesses improved - how are these assessed? What about objective data how can that contribute to this? how are players stretched and supported.

Good detail - there may need to be more ellaboration on the philosophy and club strategy found on page 1.  How does the club ensure hoolistic player developmet?  How does it ensure and indvidualised approach that is player centric?

There may need to be greater detail or more guidelines to age group coaches within these documents as to what they need to check off with their players.  Ie How do they complete player assessment that informs IDP ? Can they use objective data if so how? what does this look like?

There may need to be more detail around how the IDP are brought to life by age group coaches within sessions an dor on game day.  There may need to be more guidance for coaches as to how they assess the players and how that would then relate to IDPs based upon what the club is looking for per age and stage.

There needs to be a lot more detail about when the DIPs are crompleted and by whom?  There may need to be more guidance for coaches as to how to judge what a 1-5 player is per area of assessment - is there any scoring edcuation at the club,  The way in which the IDP is impacted must be considered in a variety fo training modalities.

There may need to be greater guidance as to how players are assessed leading into the creation on IDPs.  Seems to be a lot placed on what the players thing about their own performance.  What metrics are used for assessing players by coaches or tech leads? Is this objective data? or a scale?  How are these scores moderated through the club.  How does the club do an overarching review of how well the indivdiuals are being developed according to these action plans?

There may need to be greater guidance as to how players are assessed leading into the creation on IDPs.  There may need to be some more working docs for the club to show age group coaches how they assess per age and stage.  What one coache may see as a top performer may be different to anothet coach.

Good information but there needs to be more detail listed as to how the age group coaches complete the player assessment.  There may need to be more guidance for the age group coaches as to how they score on what scale?  How is this moderated to remove bias?

I could not see any document that gives a guideline or summary as to how the club aims to develop individual players.  Whilst there were some evidence of action being taken such as self assessment there is no document that binds this process together
There may need to be some guidance within this document whom is responsible for the completion of IDP and ensuring that both team and individualised training relates back to said IDPs.

There may need to be more guidance for what a 1-5 rating poor to excellent looks like in each of the 1-9 areas of assessnet for a player.  Whilst there is a tool to capture this through XPS the data out which informs training programs needs thave more quality.  Or at least a quality / moderation to avoid coach bias.  If objective data is used how and what does this look like?

The club’s Goalkeeping Development Strategy is well-organised, easy to navigate, and follows a logical structure that clearly outlines the club’s approach to goalkeeper development. There is an excellent level of alignment between the goalkeeping framework and the club’s overall playing style, game model, and development philosophy, with a clearly defined set of goalkeeping principles that support the club’s identity and provide consistency across the programme.

The match-day feedback process is a particular strength, with a clear framework that incorporates goalkeeper self-reflection and demonstrates how feedback is captured, reviewed, and linked to ongoing player development. The Head Goalkeeper Coach is clearly embedded within the technical staff structure, supporting collaboration across the academy and ensuring an appropriate player-to-coach ratio that facilitates individualised goalkeeper development.

While the document has continued to evolve positively, Criterion 2 remains an area for further development. The strategy would benefit from greater detail around age- and stage-specific expectations, particularly relating to the technical-tactical, psychosocial, and physical development outcomes expected at each phase of the goalkeeper pathway. Providing clearer developmental benchmarks would strengthen alignment between planning, delivery, and player progression.

Additionally, while the match-day feedback process is well articulated, the training feedback process is less clearly defined. Further detail on how formal and informal training feedback is delivered, documented, and connected to individual development plans would provide greater clarity and demonstrate a more comprehensive approach to ongoing goalkeeper development and evaluation.

The club has produced a  well-structured Goalkeeping Development Strategy that is easy to navigate and follows a logical progression throughout. The document clearly articulates the club’s vision for goalkeeper development and provides a strong framework to guide coaching practice across the academy.

A particular strength of the strategy is the level of detail provided around age- and stage-specific development. Clear consideration has been given to the technical-tactical, psychosocial, and physical requirements of goalkeepers at each phase of the pathway, providing coaches with a strong reference point for planning and player development. The strategy also establishes a distinct set of goalkeeping principles that are highly aligned to the club’s overall playing style and development philosophy, creating a clear and consistent identity for goalkeepers across all age groups.

The organisational structure outlined within the document further supports effective goalkeeper development. The Head Goalkeeper Coach is positioned as an integral member of the technical staff, ensuring alignment between the goalkeeping programme and the wider football department. The player-to-coach ratio outlined within the strategy demonstrates a commitment to providing goalkeepers with sufficient individual attention and support throughout their development journey.

While there is reference to a match-day feedback process within the document, the information provided focuses primarily on what feedback is reviewed rather than clearly outlining how the process is implemented. Further detail around the mechanisms used to capture, deliver, record, and review feedback would strengthen this area and provide greater clarity around how match-day observations are linked to individual development plans and ongoing evaluations. 

Similarly, limited information is provided regarding the training feedback process. Further elaboration on both formal and informal training feedback practices, including how feedback is communicated to goalkeepers and integrated into the individual development planning process, would enhance the overall strategy and demonstrate a more holistic approach to player development and monitoring. There is specific feedback processes provided in P4 documentation however there is a lack of GK specific processes. Feedback processes are all tailored to outfield players with the individual development coaches all outfield specific 

Overall, the club has established a strong goalkeeper development framework with excellent alignment to its playing philosophy and clear developmental guidelines. Further detail around the implementation of feedback processes would strengthen the strategy and provide greater evidence of how player development is monitored and supported on a day-to-day basis.

The club’s Goalkeeping Development Strategy provides a comprehensive overview of the key components required to support goalkeeper development within the academy environment. The document addresses all core areas, including programme structure, developmental guidelines, goalkeeping principles, feedback processes, and staffing arrangements, providing a clear understanding of what is included within the club’s goalkeeper pathway.

The strategy demonstrates alignment between the goalkeeping programme and the club’s wider playing style and development philosophy, while also outlining age- and stage-specific considerations across the technical-tactical, psychosocial, and physical domains. The role of the Head Goalkeeper Coach within the technical staff structure is clearly defined, and the document outlines the processes intended to support goalkeeper development and evaluation.

While the strategy successfully identifies the key elements of the goalkeeper programme, there is an opportunity to further strengthen the document through greater detail around the implementation of these areas. In many instances, the document clearly outlines what is being delivered, but provides limited explanation of how these processes are enacted in practice and why they have been selected as the preferred approach.

This is particularly evident within the feedback and development processes, where the intended outcomes are clear, but further detail regarding the mechanisms, workflows, responsibilities, and timelines involved would provide greater clarity and consistency for coaches and players. Similarly, while the developmental framework and goalkeeping principles are well established, additional explanation around how these principles influence session design, coaching interventions, player evaluation, and progression through the pathway would strengthen the overall strategy. Evidence is provided of reports which highlight a significant investment of time to the delivery and implementation of reports however the process can be clearer.

Providing greater insight into the rationale behind key decisions and methodologies would also enhance the document. Articulating why specific developmental priorities, coaching approaches, and feedback processes have been adopted would further demonstrate alignment with the club’s philosophy and help create a stronger connection between the strategic intent and day-to-day practice.

Overall, the club has established a solid foundation across all assessment criteria and demonstrates a clear understanding of the key components required within an effective goalkeeper development programme. The next stage of development should focus on expanding the detail around the "how" and "why" behind these processes to provide greater clarity, consistency, and practical guidance for implementation across the academy.

The club has developed a highly comprehensive and well-considered Goalkeeping Development Strategy that demonstrates a clear commitment to the long-term development of goalkeepers across all stages of the pathway. The document is exceptionally well-organised, easy to navigate, and follows a logical structure that allows key information to be easily accessed and understood by all stakeholders.

A significant strength of the strategy is the detailed articulation of age- and stage-specific development expectations. The framework clearly outlines the technical-tactical, psychosocial, and physical priorities relevant to each phase of the goalkeeper pathway, providing coaches with a strong foundation for planning, delivery, and player evaluation. This ensures that goalkeeper development is appropriately aligned with the needs of the player at each stage of their progression.

The goalkeeping development strategy establishes a distinct set of goalkeeping principles that are strongly aligned with the club’s overall playing style and development philosophy. These principles are consistently embedded throughout the document and provide a clear identity for goalkeeper development within the club. The alignment between the goalkeeping programme and the wider football methodology creates a cohesive development environment and ensures goalkeepers are prepared to fulfil the specific demands of the club’s game model.

The feedback and player review processes outlined within the strategy are another notable strength. Clear systems are in place for both formal and informal feedback relating to training and match-day performance. The document demonstrates how observations and evaluations are linked to individual development plans, ensuring that feedback is purposeful, measurable, and directly connected to ongoing player progression. The integration of review processes, reflection opportunities, and development planning provides a robust framework for supporting continuous improvement.

The staffing structure further reinforces the quality of the programme. The Head Goalkeeper Coach is clearly positioned as an integral member of the technical staff and plays a central role in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of goalkeeper development. The player-to-coach ratio outlined within the strategy reflects best practice and supports the provision of individualised coaching, feedback, and development opportunities across the academy.

Overall, the club has established a goalkeeper development framework that is comprehensive, aligned, and clearly connected to its broader football philosophy. The strategy provides a strong balance between long-term player development, coaching methodology, performance support, and operational structure. The level of detail throughout the document demonstrates a mature and well-developed approach to goalkeeper development and provides a strong platform for the continued growth and success of goalkeepers within the programme.

The club’s Goalkeeping Development Strategy provides a clear and well-structured overview of its goalkeeper programme. The document is organised logically, making it easy to navigate and understand, while outlining the key components required to support goalkeeper development throughout the academy pathway. The inclusion of age- and stage-specific considerations across the technical-tactical, psychosocial, and physical domains provides a useful framework for coaches and players and demonstrates an understanding of the developmental needs of goalkeepers at different stages of their journey.

The strategy also outlines the role of the Head Goalkeeper Coach within the academy structure and highlights the importance of goalkeeper development within the wider technical programme. The staffing model and coach-to-player ratios indicate a commitment to providing appropriate levels of support and individual attention to goalkeepers across the pathway.

While not explicitly stated within this document there is greater detail around how goalkeeper development is specifically aligned to the club’s playing model within P3. 

Similarly, while there is reference to player feedback and development processes, additional detail is required regarding how training and match-day feedback is captured, delivered, and integrated into Individual Learning Plans (ILPs). The document identifies the importance of feedback but provides limited information on the practical processes used to ensure observations from both training and competition directly inform player development priorities, action plans, and ongoing evaluations. Establishing a clearer feedback cycle that demonstrates the connection between performance analysis, coach feedback, player reflection, and ILP objectives would enhance accountability and provide greater evidence of a holistic player development framework.

Overall, the strategy establishes a solid foundation for goalkeeper development and addresses many of the key components required within an effective academy programme. Further detail around the specific role of the goalkeeper within the club’s playing model and the practical application of feedback processes linked to ILPs would strengthen the document and provide greater clarity for coaches, players, and stakeholders.

The club has developed a comprehensive and well-considered Goalkeeping Development Strategy that effectively addresses all six assessment criteria. The document is well-organised, easy to navigate, and follows a logical structure that clearly communicates the club’s vision, philosophy, and operational approach to goalkeeper development. The planning strategy provides a strong foundation for the consistent development of goalkeepers across both the men’s and women’s programmes.

A particular strength of the strategy is the level of consideration given to age- and stage-specific development. The document clearly outlines the technical-tactical, psychosocial, and physical priorities relevant to each phase of the goalkeeper pathway, ensuring that development expectations are aligned with the needs and capabilities of players at different stages of maturation. The inclusion of training considerations and adjustments across age groups demonstrates a thoughtful and player-centred approach to long-term development.

The goalkeeping principles are clearly defined and show strong alignment with the club’s broader playing style and football philosophy. This alignment provides a clear identity for goalkeeper development and ensures consistency between the expectations placed upon goalkeepers and the wider tactical requirements of the team. The framework successfully connects goalkeeper development with the overall game model, creating a cohesive approach across the programme.

The club has developed a comprehensive and well-structured Goalkeeping Development Strategy that successfully addresses the majority of the assessment criteria. The document is clearly organised, easy to navigate, and follows a logical progression that effectively communicates the club’s philosophy, development framework, and operational processes. The strategy demonstrates a strong commitment to goalkeeper development and provides clear alignment between the goalkeeping programme and the wider football philosophy of the club.

A notable strength of the document is the establishment of a distinct set of goalkeeping principles that align closely with the club’s playing style and development model. These principles are consistently reflected throughout the strategy and provide a clear framework for the development of goalkeepers within the club environment. The integration of formal and informal feedback processes for both training and match-day performance is also well articulated, with clear links to player reviews, individual development planning, and ongoing evaluation. These processes provide a strong foundation for supporting player progression and continuous improvement.
The Head Goalkeeper Coach is clearly positioned as an integral member of the technical staff, ensuring alignment between the goalkeeper programme and the wider football department. The player-to-coach ratio demonstrates an appropriate commitment to providing individualised support and development opportunities for goalkeepers throughout the pathway.

While the club’s adoption of ecological dynamics as a guiding principle for goalkeeper development is a positive aspect of the strategy, the document outlines an overarching approach to learning and player development, there is limited detail regarding age- and stage-specific guidelines across the technical-tactical, psychosocial, and physical domains. The inclusion of these developmental benchmarks remains important, even within an ecological dynamics framework, as they provide clarity around the progression of learning experiences and help guide coaching decisions regarding what actions, behaviours, and game situations should be prioritised at different stages of development.

Further age- and stage-specific guidance would also strengthen alignment between the club’s goalkeeper Individual Development Plan (IDP) framework and its assessment processes. Clearly defined developmental expectations and competencies at each stage would provide coaches with greater clarity when identifying priorities, evaluating performance, and measuring progression against agreed learning outcomes. This would ensure greater consistency across the programme while maintaining the flexibility and player-centred nature of the club’s ecological approach.

Overall, the club has established a strong goalkeeper development framework that demonstrates clear alignment with contemporary learning principles and effective development practices. The addition of more detailed age- and stage-specific developmental guidelines would further strengthen the strategy by enhancing the connection between coaching practice, assessment competencies, and individual player development planning.

The document requires refinement to present a more concise and focused overview that clearly outlines the key information related to the club’s goal-setting and Individual Development Plan (IDP) reporting process.
At present, large sections of the document are more closely aligned with P4 Individualised Planning Guidelines rather than the specific requirements of this criterion. To improve clarity and alignment, it is recommended that the club streamline the content to ensure relevance and precision.

Planning and Delivery, and
Player Reporting Process.

The document outlines a range of wellbeing strategies, including social, cultural, physical, psychological, and financial support. The club has two Education Officers responsible for academic support where required. Overall, improved document organisation and clearer role descriptions would strengthen implementation clarity and accountability.

Document is contains a lot of irrelevant information to this line item, including some double up of slides, a definite area of improvement. MCE have provided evidence of their data capturing process for injury prevention and workload tracking. Nathan Yoon is responsible for monitoring to ensure that best practice is happening throughout the whole club, however on slide 2-5 of their document it looks like he is predominantly overseeing the clubs RTP process and injury prevention. There is mention of workload tracking multiple times throuhgout the document which from the evidence provided mainly seems to be around their capturing of the data, and less about how the data is then utilised to inform decisions for the technical staff around individual players. After looking over their session plan library, training cycles and coach education workshops for the year, there is no additional support for coaches around training load periodisation and communication around personal workload targets with top-up or deloading discussed from S&C to coaches/players.

GCK have provided good detail around certain apects of how they monitor player worload tracking, predominantly though this is something that is done on an ad-hoc basis and not with appropriate emphasis on accuracy of data. XPS is used however there is little information on how the data captured from XPS influences the training and match loads of players and no evidence provided of this happening. The planning documents suppplied in P07 around their weekly schedule account for a 1-5 scale for workload which is colour coded with 5 being the heaviest load. There is however no evidence of how this changes to provided an annual periodisation that includes appropriate planning of workload management.

Lions have provided a username and password to an athlete management system, but failed to actually supply which system is used. Beyond this they have a forward planner where players are given the opportunity to supply information on what they have coming up in the next week which coaches can then use to adjust their training sessions based around this information, however it doesn't have any information about what this process looks like for coaches or any evidence of sessions that have changed based around this "planner."
There is no evidence of appropriate data caputuring methods being used around either RPE or GPS data, no evidence of education given to coaches around how to implement this information appropriately and weekly planned averages for training loads based around any periodisation is not supplied in any planning or delivery documents.

No documents submitted currently, have looked through all other documents in their planning that could assist with scoring but was unable to find what AMS platform the club uses. Have asked GG for more information.

Brisbane City have provided a good level of depth throughout their planning and delivery around their Workload Tracking and the holistic approach of the club. They use RPE data through Lumin to inform them of acute training load spikes or dips and have a red-flag system in place for when this happens and how they then work with the individual to ensure they are appropriately loaded. It isn't clear who makes the decisions or if there is any education given to coaches on how this data is used/adapted for their training sessions and daily planning, however it is evident that it currently takes place at the club. 
The one thing for the club to consider beyond evidence of coach education around adaptability of individuals/teams on workload management, would be to include targeted weekly loads for each team to ensure that appropriate preiodisation is applied for best-practice injury prevention.

Based upon the evidence provided in the powerpoint from Olympic, they have given a good level of detail on their capturing and implementation of an individualised approach to workload management through workload tracking. The concern from a data point of view, is the lack of stress on the input of ALL activities outside of the club. The data is pointless if this is not constantly being input during this process.  
Another consideration is information around how the club utilises a specific high performance periodisation in their planning to ensure that there is a target per week for the units the players in ages/stages should be hitting. Additonally information around how their coaches receive education on how to read/utilise/implement based on the individual players data.

Easts have provided a good level of detail around their ability to record, maintain and utilise their workload tracking data. While they have supplied information on each age group through their spreadsheets, the main concern is the quality of information provided through the spreadsheets. a lot of players across multiple teams have not reported at all throughout the season based on the data provided, which means that there is no possibility for the data to be utilised appropriately for training/game purposes or the ability to influence players effectively through a case-by-case basis.

While GCU have provided a very high level of detail around their S&C support and High Performance processes, there is detail missing around how coaches receive education on how to utilise data from workload tracking to ensure that sessions cater for individual workload management. Additionally there is no evidence of how workloads are planned through an appropriate periodisation model to ensure that there is loading and deloading weeks which aim to keep players progressing while still being within the acute limits of their chronic loading. No evidence was also provided around how players have been effected by the processes of the club with information aorund when/why/how they were either topped up or pulled back to hit specific loads.

Wynnum have provided information around their tracking, planning and management of player workload data. They use XPS and have identified appropriate loading goals in their annual periodisation plan, along with rough guidelines of what each sessions target RPE is. There is no mention of formalised education for coaches on how to utilise this data on a daily planning basis for modifying individual loads based on over/underloading them. Additionally something for the club to consider is showing evidence of when players have been topped up or deloaded based on the information provided through XPS.

Rochedale Rovers have submitted information around their processes for workload tracking of their players, along with their high performance support through testing. For future submissions a consideration should be adding in examples of ALL age groups data, along with any information around how this is used specifically with individual players on a case-by-case basis. There is no evidence of weekly averages being planned out for in the annual periodisation, along with evidence of how the club educates their coaches on how to use the data to top-up or deload an individual player thoroughout their weekly training sessions.

HPH have provided a good level of detail around their clubs workload tracking and management systems. They use XPS which records their players internal and external training loads, as well as do workshops with their coaches and high performance staff to ensure that they have the correct tools neccessary to make informed decisions on their players through workload management. To score higher in this area HPH should consider adding in evidence of players who have been identified as over/under loaded, as well as what was done to ensure that their workload was brought into safe margins for that week. Additionally something to consider for 2027 is how they might use workload periodisation planning to ensure that their weekly workload targets are hit and appropriate.

Magic have provided proof of the use of XPS to track their athletes workloads. Things to consider for 2027 would be how the data is able to be utilised by coaches in their day-to-day planning to ensure that players are in line for hitting their targets for the week, including communication on their monitoring and implementation of changes for that individual. Additionally there is no relevant information around their use of planning workload periodisation in their documents.

Mitchelton have provided a good level of detail around their use of XPS for their workload management system and how it aligns with their principles of periodisation for each age at the club. There is no evidence of any workload periodisation in place within the clubs planning documents and records have not been provided for each age/stage that are up to date.

Additionally there is no evidence that individuals have been impacted by their processes through top-up or pull-backs as required with personal workloads targets being set and monitored.

One thing for consideration in 2027 is the addition of evidence around individual players that have been impacted by their processes positively with records of the communication/individual workload targets and the monitoring of it until the player is back within range.

Caboolutre have provided good detail around their data capturing methods for workload management. Taringa have provided some information as to how they try to capture and use workload management data. Redlands currently could use XPS for their workload capturing and management, however this year it doesn't seem to be measured or asked by the club for information to be put in after each activity (at or away from the club) that players do.
