SSE have provided a snapshot of their lumin data for players in different ages/genders at their club. Ideally for 2027 a login should be provided for CDA's so we can look at the data across the full season. Another suggestion for 2027 would be to not just have sRPE submitted by players, but also ALL physical activity submitted, as this will lead to the data actually being useful at all. 
There is no evidence of education being provided to coaches on how to read/implement changes based upon the data provided for their daily planning, as well as no planning through their preiodisation information around planned targets and how they relate to an appropriate form of annual workload periodisation.

SWQ Thunder have provided evidence of their workload tracking and management through lumin excel data, which is then translated into the PLEASE DOWNLOAD - SWQ Thunder FC - Workload Dashboard.html file. Coaches have received infomration on how to read/utilise the data in their training/match environments through a workshop that I delivered for all of the club coaches earlier in the year. They have also provided evidence of how individuals have been managed based on their red-flag system. Considerations might be around a better implementation of the targeted weekly loads through a periodisation model which is appropriate for football in 2027.

Robina have provided access to XPS which satisfies Criteria 1-3. There is no additional information on if they've educated coaches on how to read/utilise the data from this to enhance their daily planning routine, as well is if it has ever been implemented based on a player who is over/underloaded along with adjusted targets for their weekly load. Another consideration for 2027 would be the planning of target workloads weekly by utilising a workload periodisation as part of their annual training planning to ensure that there are specific targets for players to hit.

MCE have provided screenshots and data exports from Lumin which is where they keep all of their wellbeing and workload management data. They have a qualified wellbeing officer who the players have access to and visca-versca. The only thing to consider adding would be some form of position description to the club wellbeing officer role as I couldn't find one in any of the documents.

GCK have provided information around their wellbeing officer, along with wellbeing records for each age group and their red flag system. Things to consider for 2027 would be having a PD attached for the role of club wellbeing officer with clarity around the processes required on a daily basis, as well as more information on player/parent workshops/seminars that are run around athlete wellbeing elements.

Lions have provided a well rounded document with supporting evidence on their wellbeing monitoring process at the club. One thing that Lions should include in the 2027 submission is all relevant qualifications that their club wellbeing officer has. Additionally parent/player education sessions around elements of wellbeing have not been submitted as evidence.

Logan lightning have provided good evidence around their wellbeing monitoring structures for 2026. They have a member of staff who has a degree in Special Education which involves elements of psychology, however she is also the founder of a company that has the ability to support athletes throughout the year. Something to consider is multiple sessions throughout the year on different elements of wellbeing for parents/playersr to attend to help support them in the future.

Olympic have provided a good level of evidence to meet all criteria for wellbeing monitoring.  They use XPS to get players to input their data, and their wellbeing officer then has the ability to look over it and raise red flags with the appropriate parties. There is a clear PD for them and the club has a good amount of data in their reports for most teams.

Easts utilise Lumin for their wellbeing tracking  data. They have Freya as their wellfare officer who is currently studying a bachelor of psychology (noted she has mental health awareness training and child safeguarding training currently.) They have evidence of workshops/seminars that support players and parents at the club, as well as clear evidence of communication on red flags for different elements of wellbeing throughout the year.

GCU have a wellbeing reporting system availaable through XPS, however there is very little evidence of the club actively using the platform and having players use it to report their wellbeing scores. They have Dr Jeff Kemp as their head of wellbeing, however there is no evidence of them actively engaging with red-flag reports at the club. The information provided on the GCU Wellness Hub is of a good level however.

Wolves have provided information on their exported data from an app which shows each players wellbeing information. They employ Jacob Krayem full time but I'm unsure if he has relevant qualifications or is more just another high performance physio? There is no evidence provided of how the red flags have been raised through any form of process which is something recommended for 2027.

Rochedale have provided information on their app of choice for wellbeing which is Isports, however the data provided is limited and there is only a brief mention of the information provided by players, along with a brief mention of the red-flag process, with no cases given where red flags have been raised throuhgout the year.

XPS access has been provided, but there is no data on any players readiness which is how they cover wellbeing monitoring. Their processes seem like they will work ok once there is someone that is able to monitor the players across the board, however there is no data in there so no ability for anyone to monitor or raise red flags given as evidence for this line item.
As there is no data given by ANY player that I can see in XPS, I have scored a 0 for the players ability to access the platform on criteria 3.

Magic United use XPS for their wellbeing monitoring, there is a red flag system in place however there is no information given around who is responsible for the monitoring and raising of the red flags with the appropriate parties. There is some evidence of workshops/seminars being done for parents/players, however more information and dates of workshops with attendance records should be provided in future submissions to avoid losing points in this area for 2027.

Mitchelton have provided access to XPS which is where they provide their information on wellbeing monitoring. There is a good level of data input and they have done enough parent/player workshops for it to be scored for that area. While they have appointed Anna Davis as their Wellbeing officer, there is no evidence of her qualifications or the contact information for her being shared with the players/parents.

Strikers have provided good insight into their wellbeing monitoring and how the club utilises this data. Based off of how they then potentially utilise this data as an ad-hoc system which could limit the readiness the staff have to address certain situations with players in a practical sense. The Data provided seems scarce from some teams which is something the club should improve on for 2027.

SCW have provided excellent information around all areas of the wellbeing monitoring criteria, and followed it up with evidence of it in action. They show a clear process for communication channels between the wellbeing officer and the support staff of the club along with workshop information.

Ipswich Knights have provided access to their portal which gives good information on their data collection process for wellbeing. There however doesn't seem to be much information input by players across the whole program which is something to consider working on for 2027. All players have access to this system, however it seems to be a lower priority for the club.

Cabouolture have provided their XPS login which can be used to monitor daily wellbeing questions, however there is no evidence of this being done by the club for 2026. This then limits our ability to discern if the red flag systems are appropriate for scoring in additional areas.

Virginia have given access to their data with XPS. They've had roughly 50% of their players in the last week use this for wellbeing data submissions in the last 7 days. The system is able to flag changes in players wellbeing automatically based off of previous submission data for each player, with escalation processes outlined in their documentation.

Taringa have provided access to XPS, however there seems to be a low submission rate for their players so far for this month. Ideally this will be something within the process that the club looks to improve for 2027 as without this data it becomes very subjective for what is able to be picked up on by coaches/support staff. The club has provided evidence of workshops being delivered to parents/players to support them.

Pen power have provided good information in their document of their collection of wellbeing data through XPS, as well as their red flag system on their D03 - Wellbeing Monitoring.pdf document. They have appropriate staff monitoring and communicating within their club. They have mentioned a heap of workshops for parents/players in their D21 submission, however without any evidence of these workshops taking place there was no score given for that line-item.

Samford have provided a good level of detail in their data capturing and red flag processes through XPS for their wellbeing monitoring. They have appropriate staff in place and are able to offer a comprehensive guide to their implementation of player/parent/coach education on wellbeing and welfare. One of the best systems in place across the board as it offers a long term approach and key information for all parties.

Grange Thistle use XPS to capture their players wellbeing data, however the uptake on it is very low and means that it is not being implemented properly for the club. They have provided a good amount of information through workshops, handouts and presentations for players/parents on multiple areas of wellbeing. More information is required around the clubs red-flag process and proof of communication opportunities for parents/players to reach out to the wellbeing officer.

IFC have provided an export of their Lumin data for wellbeing monitoring. Their planning documents state a position description for the club wellbeing officer. Their red-flag process seems to be driven by subjective matters and not by any of the data they collect through lumin, it says their staff are trained in being vigilant with what they identify as red-flags, however most of these can be very difficult to see from the brief interactions the staff have with players.

Capalaba use XPS to caputre their players data for wellbeing monitoring. There seems to be fairly low uptake on consistent reporting from most players, which is something the club should look to work on for 2027. There is no information about the wellbeing officers contacts being shown/given to parents/players through the induction or on the club website. Additionally there is not enough evidence of the parent/player wellbeing workshops throughout the year for any score in this area.

The Gap have provided a very comprehensive submission for their wellbeing monitoring. They capture their data through XPS and are able to upskill coaches to understand the basics, which helps to reduce the broader load on their wellbeing officers day-to-day tasks which can lead to them being able to focus more on the individuals that might require more help. I would argue that potentially there could be more evidence of workshops for 2027.

North Lakes have provided comprehensive evidence in their submission of the processes they have in place for their wellbeing monitoring. Players submit their data through XPS and they have a red-flag system in place through a flowchart. There should be a higher level of submissions by players through the app which will lead to the support staff being able to be more proactive with their ability to work with the players/parents on certain aspects of wellbeing.

Redlands have provided a brief document with a rundown of the current processes in place around their recording and use of wellbeing monitoring data through XPS. There is no mention of having a wellbeing officer with relevant qualifications listed in place, and not enough information on their red-flag system processes for points in that area.

North Star have provided information on their current capturing process for wellbeing monitoirng. The club use Lumin and it has a standardised red-flag system in place, however one thing for the club to consider for 2027 would be the implementation of a fully fleshed out process of what is required from who based upon red-flag's appearing in the data. The club have produced a physical and psychological workshop for players/parents which were delivered on wet-weather days.

Coomera have provided submissions of their jotform submissions from players for their wellbeing monitoring. They have good processes in place for red flags, as well as a question on the jotform for if they wish to receive a call from the support staff at the club about anything. I believe there is more consideration for the club in 2027 about having specific workshops/seminars around wellbeing that branch across multiple areas.

SSE have provided some evidence around their processes for wellbeing monitoring. Most of it was done through ARC which we still have not been given access to so we can't correlate the data on there with anything and haven't been given information on each team having access to this platform. 

Priscilla got an email from the TD with a link to a new platform that the club has created themselves which seems to have good data inside it from player wellbeing monitoring, however my concern is with why this was not a part of the initial submission. 
There is no mention of a wellbeing officer or contact information readily available for parents/players, and no PD given for their wellbeing officer if there is one in place at the club. Additionally there is not a lot of evidence of wellbeing being something that is included as a priority for parent/player workshops.

SWQ Thunder have provided access to Lumin hich is what they use for wellbeing monitoring. They have very good uptake on the app for submissions, and it is something actively encouraged and discussed on club visits. Brad Morris who is their wellbeing officer is at most training sessions and happily gives his time to anyone that has questions, and also talks with coaches/players about stressors. They have had education sessions throughout the year for parents/players and have appropriate red-flag escalation processes in place.

Robina have submitted information on their wellbeing monitoring process with the use of data submission through XPS. Helen, Michael and Ethan are all listed in different presentations/planning documents as support roles, however there is not much clarity around who is responsible for what, PD's for each persons role would be helpful for 2027. Additionally there should be more consideration around the full red-flag reporting process, along with information on how parents/players are able to contact the appropriate person for their wellbeing support.

No physical testing data is detected in the Lumin system. The club has a good process description and may have data stored elsewhere as their case studies show good care of late developers and evidence based practcies.

GCK use a detailed RAE tracking to get facts about their player cohort. PHV mesures are from 2025. They list 10 strategic actions to reduce disadvantage of late born (potentially late developer) players.
The club has very detailed multi touch point PHV and physical testing documents. There are grouping of players based on bio-banding which is best practice. There were no planning document provided.

Logan Lightning has through sport science process with one PHV measurement the day. They use the data to manage players indiviudally throughout the stages and they have provided good examples of this practice in the Sports Medicine Program document.

Brisbane City provides mainly physical testing data. There is one PHV measurement provided. The SSSM process is a one page info graphic, doesn't provide clear information on varied player management or exact planning for late developers.

PHV measurements are stored in XPS. Information provides input to Sport Science and Coaching Staff, but no exact plan is submitted to provide insight how does it work within ages and stages or for late developers.

Easts repeats PHV at the first week of each month. There is a clear communication between Sport Science and Coaching Staff with a management suggestion for each players +/-6 Month of the PHV. There is only one missing element, a robust plan for late developers.

GCU has PHV measurement once a year (currently boys data is submitted). Although they have a qualified staff, there is no evidence of more measurement and individualised management of late developers. If the girls data is not provided I support Pris's score.

Wynnum has PHV testing four times a year. They follow a clear process, bio-banding groups are created from the data. More dteail would be great how the groups are working, what specific programs they provide to late developers.

Rochedale conducts 2-3 PHV testing, but girls data wasn't amongts the examples (it will be required for a three point score). The club has a communication process to manage players in peak growth stages (SSSM> coaches > parents) and they have modified gym, workload or game minute reductions. An overall club based plan wasn't provided.

PHV measurement is supposedly done three times but there is only a May 2026 record in XPS. Rate of Development criteria is met in good faith as the system provides maturity offset to SSSM staff and player (years pre/post PHV). There is an ages and stages management descriptor in their Bio Banding plan although the implementation is not proven.
Magic Unieted has two data sets on PHV in the XPS and third testing is scheduled for end of the year. They use the data to manage players, including late developers.

Mitchelton FC conducted one PHV testing in 2025. They also indicate that they do Predicted Adult Height calculation but it has no evidence. The plan provides a high level overview regarding their intent to use the data appropriately. There are no concrete actions or examples are shared in what way they support late developers.

There is many missing data points at the U13, U15, U16, U18 boys and only one PHV measurement. No data on South Strikers girls. There is no reference on who are the SSSM practitioners and only the TD mentioned who makes play up/down decisions. One example of an athlete playing down while backed with data.

SCW's PHV data collection is inconsistent as they ask players to submit their own PHV data which doesn't offer standard measurements and the frequency of players submission is also varied. There is a Coaches Guide and Mid-Season Coaches email sent by the academy administrator. While the external physio is involved in the process there is no programmed intervention, but information needs to be translated into action by indiviudal coaches which is also beyond their expertise and also inconsistent.

IK has a very robust documentation regarding the club's maturation tracking process. There is a full set of evidence of three testing periods and the data also recorded on the club's own management prortal. The club talks about bio-banded training and it is currently under checking with the CDA to see if it has been observed. Ipswich Knights is congratulated on their planning while they need to make sure that there is practical implementation of the SSSM staff's work to better support athletes.

Caboolture has only completed one PAH measurement to date this year. The TD is Sport Science qualified. There are a few ways indicated the clubs attempyts to use the data set but there is only an example of late developer twin brothers mentioned in the documentation. The club is on the right track but more frequence and resources are required to meaningfully effect the academy boys and girls program.

Virgina has a high compliance on three PHV testing for all teams  - well done. The data is stored in their XPS platform. The SSSM document provides information abut no ages and stages differentiation and no evidence of real practical implementation for late developers.

Taringa's program has a basic start in maturation measurement. Only boys teams were tested and only once this year. The first data set was collected in the second part of July which didn't leave time for any practical assessment and implementation of the findings.

Only screen shot records provide evidence of a January measurement. A SSSM professional reviewed the data and provided some info on red flags for the TD. Detailed practical implementation is missing as well as the evidence on frequence and application for all U13+ age groups.

Samford has a strong data set stored on XPS, measured in all three terms. There is a vague understanding of data usage, and superficial practical use od the findings. Keep defining the process and make it useful for the athletes.

Grange provided records of three PHV measurement but not for all age groups, only boys names in the data set. There is no plan how to use the information. The last assessed Sport Science support planning document from 2025 was checked and it doesn’t provide information on the support of late developers.

Ipswich FC has a strong compliance with three PHV testing for both genders and all age groups. Players profiling merges both maturation and physical testing considering the indiviudal and shows team's average as well. There is a descriptor for players/parents and coaches on all maturation profiles. There is also programming advise (somewhat genericc) for each cases pre, circa and post PHV.

Capalaba has sporadic PHV testing for both genders. The club phyiso assessed physical competencies but his findings mainly based on observations and physical testing instead of maturation. There is an interesting initative to affect indiviudals' needs in power, movement, speed and conditioning aspects within the Youth program. The frequency (once in a 6 week cycle) is low but players can learn training techniques to practice alone. There is no connection drawn between exercise perscription and the PHV data.

The Gap does PHV measurement, physical testing for all age groups and also checks RAE statistics. The physio provides a report on all age groups, but not on indiviudals. Physio's advice include PHV considerations in a generic manner, but there is no programming attached to the recognition.

North Lakes has a solid plan concerning their players' maturation and growth with three PHV test per year. The highlight of their plan is a parent/player info fact sheet that helps them to navigate the challenges around growth spurts. The club says IDP sessions might be grouped based on maturation but there is no evidence for the practical distinction.

Redlands United had sporadic PHV data collection (6-9 players per team) once a year so far. The club's physical testing is mainly recorded on paper that doesn't allow good data transfer. There is no programming attached to the process. Based on the submission there is no qualfied personnel oversees the data-handling.

North Star conducts PHV measurement in each three terms (first two data set is submitted). The use an "AI-tool" to analyse the data and provide recommendations. It would be recommended to cross-check this process with the club's SSSM practitioners. The listed considerations, actions (non-action decisions) and TID/retention aspects are all valid and great outcomes to make more informed decisions. Indiviudal programming is yet to be resourced.
Coomera works with a head of medical to assess maturation. PHV is measured three times a year. Indiviudalised programs and managing late developers are yet to be integral part of the process.

There is a lot of unproven planning provided. There is no PHV measurements submitted, only physical testing. Staffing and concrete actions for affected players (i.e. late developers) are both unclear.

SWQ has a well documented process. Some data set doesn't show seated height for PHV but it might only a false reading. There are two testing coducted so far and there is a good level of implementation in place. The recommednation influence coaching decisions for the most "at risk" players.

The club's Sport Science Support submission from 2025 talks about "Four-monthly anthropometric measurements" but there is no evidence of this testing. There is no such data located on the club's XPS platform either.

Moreton City has a good process for Return to play. A committed physio works on site and provides rehab for the players. Records are robust and appropriate. Historical data , concrete match minute subscription and emergency plan is missing.

GCK has an FA recommended RTP and AIS best practice based Concussion policy. The club's physio is an experienced practitioner who works with Junior Matildas. Screening records were provided at a planning line item. Medical records are not stored in XPS due to privacy. Club physio (Jess) keeps a record and records on players who see an external physio is collated by Pat offline (he is happy to sight it). There is no integrated communication in this area; storage of players injury history isn't achieved. The club focus is injury prevention in their own words. There seems to be no on field RTP provided by the club for players.

Lions FC has a fairly detailed overview on the RTP process. The club's own physio's reports and communication with external medical practitioners are provided. The AMS acess is limited to the assessor, but Dashboards are detected for Player Availability and Injury records. Given Lions use AMS for years it seems to have long term records. There is  no evidence of screening/baseline testing. Some areas partially covered (concussion Yes, EpiPen/Emergency response No). It is difficult to get a good understanding if physio and S&C contributes to RTP on field. In player presentation only a free club based Monday triage is included and 20% discount for at clinic treatment. If the screening/testing or RTP run by physio is evidenced that leads to full 3 point score.

There is strong RTP descriptor per injury types by club's physio partner. Further evidence is requested from the club and they provided evidence for injury log, communication protocol (password protected Google sheet).

Brisbane City's summary document provide a thorough process in RTP. There is a multi-disciplinary team working with the players to safely return them to play. Baseline testing/screening (mentioned in doc, examples in D4) and communication channels are established in Lumin and data recording in SharePoint. As it is a new system there is no historical injury data, a concussion/EpiPen/Defib policy was required in the descriptor and they haven't been outlined in the submission.

Olympic FC has a well thought through process about RTP. They provide education to staff and players as well within the XPS systems. Baseline testing and screening data is also stored in the online system. Although the club provides triage to juniors it is noted that Ranveer and Manali the head of men's and women's program physio communicates with external stakeholders and coordinates rehab. In the video section of the RTP submission they work with a player with an overuse injury, they retest and provide exercises to be completed at the club's on site gym. Based on the care, concrete example and the ability to do rehab on-site. The main missing component is a live communication register, online form with notes is recommended.

Eastern Suburbs FC displays a best practice medical and RTP model. They have club physio on site two nights a week, and a separate Head of Rehab is appointed with different touch points throughout the week. The screening, testing is done for all age groups. The ESFC Performance Portfolio Resource Manual is an examplary document that provides holistic information for all aspects of their Sport Science and Sports Medicine activities. Communication with schools about injured players and loading is also at a very high level. I suggets Criteria 2 & 3 is accepted and results a maximum score.

There is a good overview document as how it is planned to deliver RTP at GCU. There is little to know evidence based on the doc and XPS login regarding practical implementations. I reached out to the club TD for urgent clarification and on request we have been provided communication protocols (GCU Medical WhatsApp comms) and injury records (weekly triage summaries)

Wynnum has a well resourced RTP protocol. They use XPS, XPS Health and a weekly Excel form to also manage modified game minutes. Club physio is available on site, club has 4 S&C coaches to provide rehab trainings. There is process for emergency events and XPS health offers a good overview of the health / availability data live. Historical player injury register is a recommendation to be added.

Rochedale Rovers has simple but effective plan for RTP. The club physio provides weekly update after the Monday triage within a medical messaging platform. Sports trainers are at all trainings and games and there is a level of supervision to support RTP. Emergency protocols and training are in place. Historical injury data and more integrated on field support is recommended.

HPH use an online Excel sheet as injury and RTP register maintained by medical staff. XPS hosts player readiness and testing data. There is no exact integrated system to connect both and provide a clear, seemless communication protocol. No historical injury data and no evidence of on-field support during early stages of RTP. Good basics around emergency response.

Magic United has an integrated injury recording the RTP communication via XPS Health. It is also XPS where players first self-report injuries. There is no historical data, on field S&C support or refrence to concussion protocols. There is a yearly basline testing rec

Mitchelton's word doc provides a fair overview of their RTP framework but some evidence is not available to validated the delivery on the process. Injury records, the proof of their "integrated communication system" apart from the recently trialed but not fully utilised XPS Health module. There is some past injury updates in their screening document but it is questionable if Injury history without concrete Grade of tears and treatment plans is adequate. The January screening process seems to be thorough and covering around 100 players in the academy. Concussion, EpiPen, Defib policies are templated documents, which is acceptable although it needs to be made sure that they are embedded to coaches and members induction or at least onboarding info packs. It is also slightly unclear to what extent the club physio treats players. There is a triage process by teh physio, but actual treatment plan management is not provided. Supplementary file 1-3 is referenced but not submitted. It is requested from the club to allow an informed final decision on the extent of the RTP process.

There is a two pages process document with older files referenced from 2025 while the link is not working to access them. The Performance Management 2026 document is a tracking tool with basic details on injured players without complete information. Injury detailes are provided in a post match day or triage report where there is a description of the injury and next step advice (without treatment plans provided). There is no injury history on players, no screening results are provided. The doucments provided don't offer clarity on communication lines and practical Return To Play support. There is one case study on a player which steps listed with no author (club physio, external medical personnel?). It is also unclear if players access on site RTP S&C coaching, rehab exercises. The concussion protocol is FA's old policy document which is accepted in good faith. Detailed emergency policies are not included and generally speaking most protocols are hard to judge on based on the quality of the submission the club provided in this area. The current execution is closer to the '1' point mark and I suggest that the 3rd assessor makes a final decision.

SC Wanderers is working on a robust RTP process. They have changed their methods from form based reporting to XPS Health recording. The physio engaged with the parents in a presentation and holds triage once a week. Based on the documentation the treatment happens at Sage Physiotherapy. Reporting back to the club is more appropriate since shifting the process to XPS. There is no evidence of screening and basline testing (they are only mentioned in the summary document), it is also unclear if club S&C or Jetts Fittness provides rehab trainings to club players or is it only gym access. The club is heading to the right direction but some fine tuning is still required. Concussion protocol awareness exists, this also requires embedding into standard procedures.

IKFC has a detailed documentation with imrpoving delivery. The IKFC Portal is the main record holding hub with screening data, injury records and generic programming for individuals who did baseline testing. There are some great injury reduction rates eventated according to Year On Year statistics amongst flagged players thanks to the club's efforts. At the same time several age group has only shows 5-6 players who got through the initial testing which shows some lack of buy in. It is unclear if on-field or gym based rehab is provided. There is no reference to concussion or emergency policies.

Caboolture uses XPS Health. There is a tidy process of injury recording, monitoring and notifications. It seems to be no baseline testing, rehab is managed at external clinic. No reference to concussion policy.
XPS Health is now accessed. There are good injury records by physio and TD, injury status indication and communication with medical documents uploaded. No club based rehab, lack of concussion policy.

Taringa has a improved compliance in RTP. The club contracteded Allsports Forest Lake for triage at the club and further treatment can be booked by the player at the clinic. There were a baseline testing completed in the off-season. Injury records are regular, the Excel shows up to March records but the Word doc based has ongoing logs. A more integrated potrtal would make comms easier. Concussion and other emergency responses have generic compliance.

Basic compliance while it can improve with XPS Health introduction. There is a good notification proces but there are no injury history log from the past. No evidence of baseline tests, in-house rehab and standardised emergency responses.

Samford has great services with GP and physio triage and XPS Health recording. In my assessment there is no evidence of basline testing, the document refers to injured players testing. There are some rehab exercises provided by club based staff which is great practice. Ongoing physio comes at a discounted cost off site. Past injury data is not recorded in my understanding.
There is a basic process description on RTP. Grange use XPS to record injuries. There is no evidence of screening, on-field rehab for players and historical injury data.

Ipswich FC leaves the medical part of the RTP process outside the club's remit. External physio assesses and treats the player. The club's Head of High Performance, Lleyton collates advise, translates it into actionable items for coaches and manages workload. There is a concussion policy in place and a few cases presented how did the club manage RTP with the above framework. There is no screening, triage, injury history, on field rehab evidenced.

Capalaba's RTP submission was difficult to navigate with many indiviudal physio reports uploaded beside process documentation.The club use XPS, WhatsApp for recording and communication. Injury history is recorded for the last two years in a master file. No screening, on site rehab. Concussion policy exists.

The Gap FC has a thorough process, they use the Lumin App, involve the club physio, wellbeing officer and TD. The only missing element is that their physio or S&C don't treat players. There is only triage at the club. At the pre-season testing and screening they record existing / past injuries and their process document states that the club keeps records for 5 years.

North Lakes use XPS Health for injury recording and they have qualified staff with clear responsibilities. The physio holds club based triage but on site rehab is unclear. The club conducts testing, but there is no evidence of screening. There is a concussion protocol and they aim to store historical injury data in XPS.

Redlands has a valid screening and testing prtocol at the beginning of the season. Players access sport trainers at games and they can be triaged by physio if they get injured. There is no central location for injury reports and rehab plans. No concussion or emergency response policy.

North Star has a logical process in RTP. There is good historical data on injury triage records from 2024 to date. There is no evidence of on site rehab amd programming. There is physical testing for fitness but there is no pre-season screening for injury prevention.

Coomera has improved the process for RTP. All return to play goes through the club physio at the complementary triage night which makes it a one stop shop. Injury form and wellbeing monitoring complements this process. There is no screening, concussion/emergency management policy and evidence for on-site rehab. There are process documents available for members.

SSE outsource their medical process to Motion Health which company offer free triage at their clinic where they assess or clear players to return. MH also holds records and communicates with cosches. Rehab programming is at the players cost with some discount from MH. There is no club based rehab, no evidence of concussion policy, emergency management plan, physio screening.

SWQ Thunder has a best practice Process documentation for all areas of RTP. Records are kept in Lumin App including screening and injury list. High and consistent level of delivery of training sessions. This is thanks to the high level of planning of the TD/TLs. In the female space and in the 2nd teams there is room for improvement. It would be great to invest in assistant coaches as sometimes the ratio players/coaches is still too high. Yet, one of the best academy in the State.

The club works with experienced and qualifed coaches. Scott McDonald is head of Youth but also the U14 coach. He attempted to share his methdology tweeks at rotational sessions with the U13 to U15 age groups. Strong coaches positively influence players learning in the boys space, but more alignement is needed. The girls academy is led by Elisa Brito who support coaches in person, while some more alignement is required between the two genders.

There has been a much improved overally delivery at the club in 2026. Consistency in training organisation and delivery has been added, which has added to the increase in standards in the program. The next step is to continue to work to ensure that all ages and phases are completely aligned in delivering the methodology.

Logan has displayed good improvement with the Strike/Spark methodology. After Gary's departure who created the program's blueprint may have been less follow up on the implementation of the training delivery.

There is still a disparity at the club between delivery in the junior age-groups and the youth age-groups. This was mentioned in last year's assessment and full marks won't be able to be achieved in this line item until delivery in the boys and girls youth age-groups reflects the juniors.

The structure of all sessions is good.  The TD has a close eye on session delivery and or its content as do the other supporting lead coaches.  There may need to b some greater detail offered by lead support staff across fewer teams. Coaches may need to focus on ensuring that the real aim of the session is completed not simply to get through all of the component areas of the session plan.  IE if players are struggling they may need longer on a session type / drill.  If they are thriving they may need to move on quicker.

Great improvements in the last couple of years at the Club with investments in resources to deliver the program. Training observation is consistently good with TD and TLs always present to support coaches and players. It is to be mentioned that the club differentiate itself from a good delivery in both male and female programs.

The GCU trainings delivered within the club's expectations, closely monitored by Jamie Dixon and phase leads, plans are also provided. Coaches ogranisation and overall conduct is good. There some inconsistencies with the methodology and understanding details. Post training evaluation is not always delievered.

Session delivery is generally good including GKS and Individualised sessions.  Coaches may need to think about their intervention types and the way they impart knowledge on players.  It may be that the coaching methodology needs better delivery.  Some sessions tend to be delivered in terms of ongoing practices with coaching 'in the breaks'  a more common appraoch then would be detailed in the coaching methodology.

Training delivery observations at the club have been fine. There is clear intent from most of the coaches to follow a prescribed plan and to allow maximum ball rolling time throughout the sessions(This was feedback from 2025) Coaches football knowledge is at a decent level which has allowed this to happen. The score is a touch above a 3 but definitely not a 4.

Training delivery is in line with previous years. Overall, the training are organisedwith some sessions better than others, mainly due to the different level of experience. There are inconsistencies across different phases or age groups; coaches inonsistently display the outlined criteria. 
Based on the limited amount of observations, I believe there there is scope for the TD to be more influencial towards some of the coaches on the field in the next season.

Jake Goodship has positively changed the overall picture of the Training Deliveries - marked improvement is visible in the Junior boys and Youth boys program. Technical detail is evident in planning and execution. The coaches apperance and behaviour is also positive.

With only limited observations completed, as I became the CDA very late in this season, Mitchelton shows some positive foundations in its training environment. New Technical Director Sam has an opportunity to establish clearer direction and greater consistency across the programme, but needs to be more 'hands on'. Further observation and assessment by the CD Unit may be required to provide a clearer and more accurate score, particularly across planning, coaching interventions, feedback, and shared session resources. The Female Program requires further support, as it currently appears to operate in silos. Greater connection with the wider club methodology, coaching framework, and shared planning processes would help create a more consistent player-development experience across the programme.
I have observed a number of training sessions and game day visits this season since GT left. I am happy to be challenged on this by the second assessor.

Overall, there is consistency across the junior and youth phases in coaching methodology and training cycles. All youth teams have a minimum of a half-pitch activity and technical coaching related to the session topic; however, some coaches lack coaching detail. There are no clear post-session reviews at the end of sessions, with teams moving straight into cool-down and pack-up mode.

Overall, there is a consistent club-wide approach to the training structure. All teams follow the training cycles and topics outlined in their weekly plans. In the Junior Phase, some coaches are more facilitative in their approach and run good sessions. The next step is to identify key moments to deliver effective coaching points that maximise player learning and development.

Overall, there is a strong and consistent club-wide approach to training delivery, with all coaches following the club’s methodology, training cycles, and session plans. Sessions were well organised, game-based, and provided high levels of active learning time in a positive learning environment. The main development area is increasing age-appropriate differentiation and delivering more individualised, player-specific coaching interventions to maximise player development outcomes.

Clear consistency in training topics, however coaches can be disorganised before the start of session. The loss of Steve Boxx mid season has left a hole, with one less strong coach and providing greater strain on the technical staff. There is limited technical detail, even in some junior sessions - this is an area to improve moving into 2027. Post session debrief is evident in all sessions. 

Overall greater guidance is needed in session design and content, to allow age appropriate content and feedback. Additionally, the club needs to appoint Technical Leads that are not coaching a team at the same time as other teams within its phase to allow improved delivery on the pitch.

A clear strength of the club comes from the structure and consistency of session objectives and design across teams within the same development phase. Coaches are organised, with different session structures from Play - Prac - Play, Carousel format or progressive structure. The delivery on pitch is somewhat limited by the ability and experience of the coaches, some are able to adapt whereas some struggle to change to maximise learning opportunities. There is a need for increased technical detail across all sessions, and improved quality of interventions. There is some observation of TL (Rob, Pam) and TD overseeing training sessions, but a gap in the youth due to changes during the season.

There is improvement from 2027, but just shy of a 3 due to inconsistency in quality of adaptation and interventions due to difference in coaching quality.

Clear consistent session plans for teams within the same phase, with good level of organisation throughout. There is clear objectives for both junior and youth phases, however there is an overall lack of depth in technical detail within session delivery (despite a couple of coaches displaying a good level). The Academy has a range of coaches from newer inexperienced ones to strong coaches especially within its Technical Team, and there has been a couple of changes within its coaching set up during this season, resulting in a score of 2. 

If there is improvement in the support on pitch by its Technical team, and with the growth and renewal of the coaching staff for 2027, I am confident there will be an improvement in the delivery and hence score.

While training plans are in place for all cycle and training the content of the plans are disconnected from the age group (i.e. U12B C5/W29 counter press focus for skill acquisition age) or not logically follow the main theme (i.e. U15B C4/W22 1v1 isolation topic but plan aims a 2v1/3v2 overload out wide).  Some SAP teams had set pieces /corners session at observation while other teams have done something completely different (first touch).

Criteria 2 has not been met with 100% assurance. Also 4, 5 & 7 are not at a very high level. The coaches football knowledge is average at best and they are very well intended and supported by the technical director. I have spoken with the Td and he is keen to keep all coaches onboard for 2027 simply because they have bought into the clubs philosophy and genuinely care about the clubs continued growth.

Overall, my observations of training sessions have been very positive. The areas identified for improvement in 2027 within Categories 4,5,& 6 are primarily linked to the coaches' current level of football knowledge and experience, rather than a lack of commitment or effort.

It is evident that football is being played in an engaging and enjoyable environment, with players actively participating and demonstrating enthusiasm for the game. This provides a strong foundation for future development, and I am confident that, with continued support and coach education, The Gap will continue to build on these positive outcomes in the years ahead.

North Lakes is transitioning from a community-football environment and provides generally organised, positive training sessions. With Jhonny as Technical Director and Costa as Director of Football, there is an opportunity to establish a more consistent club-wide methodology.
Further development is needed in planning, coaching interventions, observation and feedback, and shared session resources across all groups - but a great work in progress for the Club

2026 has seen a massive improvement in this item I have marked criteria 4&5 as no and been a bit harsh with this. Coaches are at a decent level with their football knowledge however, there is an inability to adjust sessions based on players ability and possibly the lack of football knowledge of some coaches. This may contradict what I have said before. I think with some more work in 2027 this can and will improve.

North Star shows  positive foundations in its training delivery, with coaches providing organised sessions and a supportive environment for players. The arrival of new Technical Director Gareth presents an opportunity to establish clearer direction and greater consistency across the programme. At present, delivery and coaching interventions are not yet consistently aligned to a clearly embedded club-wide methodology. Further work is needed around structured planning, technical detail, coach observation and feedback, session evaluation, and use of a shared electronic session library. A more consistent approach across all groups will be needed to move toward the club’s intended development standards.

There is clear consistency in the delivery as everything is planned centrally by the TD Davide. However the focus of the sessions can have inappropriately high tactical focus, even for junior phase sessions. This is exacerbated by the level of coaches at the club, who have limited knowledge in the technical aspect. 

Overall I believe there is an improvement from last year, however Davide still needs time to shape the program and improve the level of his coaches to increase the quality across the board.

SWQ Thunder have improved their coaching ranks this year with some good additions to their coaching team. Most of them are confident or gaining confidence in providing engaging intervention moments and most use the specific club wording around each of the main moments when communicating with players. A few on observation nights went into old habits and used inconsistent wording, however generally there was a good level of consistency from the coaching group.

Despite the high quality of interactions with the players, there is room for improvement with focus on consistency across both programs, and different phases. Based on observation the junior space is definitely oexcelling, compared to other phases

Craig Midgley and Scott McDonald has a very strong influence on their players and other coaches are able to learn from them and imporved their interactions. Coaches at GCK generally has a high level of interactiona and able to challenge most  players within their sessions.

There has been some positive changes made in coach interaction in 2026. With some new coaches and staff at the club, working closely with the coaches to ensure that they deliver consistently in line with the club's methodology will be important to continue to focus on moving forward.
Adding some guidelines around session differentiation will help improve individual player outcomes.
Inconsistency in differentiation and consistency. Most coaches has great manner, communicate well and intends the learning of all players.

Once again, the trainin delivery of the coaching staff in the junior age-groups is at a higher level than that in the middle to older youth age-groups. Session differentiation in the youth age-groups in particular will be important to embed player learning with technical and tactical information that is relevant to them

Coaches may need to think about the timing and type of intervention used.  There was a workshop on interventions / shared best practice in 2025 and may still be something the club looks to focus on.  The coaches observed tended to deliver coach led feedback or direct interventions.  It may be that more alignment to the coaching methodology can be foudn in more questioning and guided learning.  Even within GK sessions.  For the junior female program there may need to be more technical details shared in the sessions.  This specific area needs attention to not let coaching mostly happen 'in breaks' between practices.

There are inconsistencies across different phases or age groups; coaches inconsistently display the outlined criteria. Despite the delivery is in line with the club's coaching methodology, the different experience of the coaches and where they are at in their journey are still evident in the organisation and delivery. It is probably worth considering having the TD and TLs more involved on the field at times - finding the right balance will be key.

Coaches interaction is at a good standards. The technical team's manner, ability to motivate and teach is generally consistent, while application of differentiation and upholding the methodology isn't always. Coaches efficient following the sessions, but some of them finds it challenging when the training numbers change and they need to adapt the plans to reality - especially in the girls programs. The club's strongest point is the Junior phase where Matt and Jamie created a very good environment.

In general the coaching delivery at the club is well organised and structured. Linked to above the club is in a good space here as mentioned before BRT was highlighted and is definitely got better. I suppose the challenge for 2027 is for the coaches to prepare a script with club aligned questions to challenge the players.

Magic aims to develop their Adaptable Player ethos. Most coaches are able to modify the plans and guide players by stepping up/down difficulty while some struggles with this detail and "just running the plan". Overall it is a positive picture.

There is an opportunity to further support coaches in the areas of session planning, organisation, and delivery to maximise training efficiency. In particular, refining intervention timing and coach communication can help reduce unnecessary stoppages and increase ball rolling time, ensuring players receive more purposeful activity and engagement throughout each session.
Strikers has a specific playing style that has followed on since Nacho left. I have been generous with my scoring here based on my limited observations.observations.

The club coaching staff create a good learning environment; however, there are inconsistent levels of coaching ability across the club. There is a group of B Diploma coaches who make well-timed interventions and effectively support player development, while a group of C Diploma coaches are still learning their craft, especially in relation to implementing guided discovery methods.

Overall, coaches created a positive, engaging learning environment aligned to the club’s methodology, with high levels of active learning time and intensity. However, coaching interventions were often general in nature, with limited football-specific detail and missed opportunities to make key learning interventions linked to the PDE learning chain. The next step is to improve the delivery of clear coaching cues and identify live moments to deepen player understanding and learning

Overall, coaching delivery was aligned with the club's methodology, with coaches generally adopting a facilitative, constraints-based approach and creating positive learning environments. However, coaching interventions were limited, with few well-timed PDE coaching moments and a tendency for feedback to remain general rather than focused on specific technical details or individual player actions. While some coaches demonstrated effective intervention and detailed coaching, a greater focus on live coaching moments, clearer football pictures, and more individualised player feedback would further enhance player learning and development outcomes.

Changes within the technical staff including coaches and TD has not helped in this area. Generally less than ideal ball rolling time and effective interactions with players within the junior boys and girls program. The youth program has stronger coaches, including now the TD and DOF which puts it in a better place. Greater detail is needed throughout all interventions, including clear coaching cues and having 'live' interventions in the moment to increase effectiveness of interactions with players.

Nonetheless, there is good energy brought about by all coaches, which is a strength that should continue.

Overall the coaches at Samford are able to facilitate sessions with appropriate body language and tone, this has improved throughout the season as coaches increase in confidence. However, there is an overall lower ability to communicate effectively, using smart Q&A to influence players - interventions can be long and ball rolling time reduced. 

Some work can be done with coaches as well to adapt sessions to challenge players of varying ability at the right levels.

Generally, there is an inclusive and engaging learning environment, and coaches have positive tone and mannerism, this needs continue work to ensure that it is consistent throughout. Improvement in design and managing transitions can help with greater ball rolling time. Coaches try to ask good Q&A, however this is more evident in experienced coaches e.g. TL Liam, Fraser, and can be improved across the board.

Coaches experience wildly different: U14 boys coach with no qualification, while TD is also active with some teams and offers great support. A level of inconsistency was observable with well-mannered coaches who could rely on Sam, Vaughan or Adam's support.

Coach observation and interaction has improved in 2026. Coaches at The Gap demonstrate a sound ability to facilitate training sessions. This is not a criticism of the club but rather a reflection of the current experience, football knowledge, and stage of development of the coaching cohort.

Key areas for improvement in 2027 should focus on coach development, particularly around the effective use of interventions. Communication during sessions should be clear, concise, and purposeful, with interventions remaining relevant to the learning objective and, wherever possible, delivered while maintaining player engagement with the ball.

Greater clarity in session design is also required, including the development of specific themes, clear learning outcomes, and the consistent use of common football language throughout the program. These elements will provide coaches with a stronger framework for player development and support their own growth as practitioners.

With ongoing support, mentoring, and constructive feedback, there is every confidence that he will continue to grow and positively influence the club's coach development environment throughout 2027.

North Lakes is very invested in its programme and is progressing well, providing a generally supportive environment where coaches build positive relationships with players. The club have IDP session embbeded into there weekly trainign cyle. Overall, coaches currently do not have the skill set to consistently deliver individual player development (IPD) messages alongside team-based coaching. This is further impacted by the lack of assistant coaches regularly working with the groups to help share the coaching workload and support individual player development.

Overall, there was strong evidence of a consistent club playing model across all age groups, with teams demonstrating clear build-up patterns, controlled possession, and aligned pressing behaviours. The U14 and U15 teams consistently applied the model, while the U16s showed some tendency to play more directly at times. Common attacking and pressing principles were evident across the age groups, demonstrating strong alignment to the club's game model. While implementation was generally positive, technical execution and game understanding varied between teams and players, impacting consistency in applying the desired playing style.

The use of common football language by all coaches will be an important component of this process, helping to create alignment in coaching messages and player development outcomes.

Additionally, coaches should be encouraged to make stronger connections between training content, Individual Development Plans (IDPs), and match-day performance. Establishing this clear link between the training environment and game-day application will help maximise player development and reinforce the club's football philosophy.

Overall, a player development approach was evident, with coaches regularly reinforcing individual learning through position-specific feedback and player tasks. The strongest example was within the U15 program, where a clear team learning objective was translated into specific individual football actions for players to execute. However, there was limited evidence of formalised Individual Player Development (IPD) match objectives, evaluation processes, or tasks linked directly to each player's strengths and development areas. Most individual learning remained connected to the team model rather than personalised development goals.

Overall, match day learning was predominantly team-focused, with coaches concentrating on collective match objectives rather than individual player development outcomes. While some informal references to individual player tasks were made during team talks, there was no clear or documented process for setting, monitoring, or reviewing individual learning goals. As role models, coaches play a critical part in setting the tone for player conduct, decision-making, and emotional control during games.

The match-day environment should remain focused on supporting both team performance and individual player development. Coaches who communicate in a calm, positive, and purposeful manner create better opportunities for players to learn, make decisions, solve problems, and express themselves within the game. This is particularly important in a development-focused environment, where long-term player growth should take precedence over short-term match outcomes.

This is an area that has already been discussed with the club, and continued attention should be given to ensuring that coaches consistently model the behaviours and standards expected of players. A composed and development-focused approach from the technical area will not only enhance the match-day experience but will also contribute positively to the ongoing technical, tactical, and personal development of individual players across the club.

The U13 coach spent a large amount of time chopping and changing player positions, reducing learning time and focus. While infomation related to the match objective, it was very disjointed.

Similarly, the U14 half-time team talk didn't use the tactics board well, and had no magnets. This team talk didn't reinforce the key player actions and didn't have a clear process. This led to very disjointed player lead conversation, which were superficial and not linked to the match objective. Even though these were player-led discussions due to the nature, they weren't aligned to a PCC approach, just general player chit chat. 
Coaching behaviour was okay. Coaches mainly observed and prompted with a few key interventions. No halftime team talk no tech board use for either the under 13s or under 15s. Some good Q&A from the under 13s but the under 15s was just general information needs to be better.

Copilot said:
Overall, coaches consistently demonstrated positive, age-appropriate behaviour and created a supportive learning environment aligned with club values. Half-time discussions were generally linked to match objectives and the training cycle, with some use of Q&A and tactical boards; however, information was often general in nature and focused on team outcomes rather than individual player actions and development. The effective use of tactical boards and match picture animation was inconsistent across teams, limiting player understanding of key concepts. While coaching interactions and conduct were strong, a key development area is improving the quality and clarity of match day communication by providing more specific, player-centred learning messages and better linking team objectives to individual actions.

Match day prep and organisation is often done well, esp in warm ups. There is a need to improve in game coaching and behaviours on the sideline including half time and post game interactions to maximise learning - that said there are definitely some coaches that have good interaction with players at half time which is commendable. There are some lengthy post game debriefs which may not aid learning.

Half time team talks were generally good - they were very heavily team focused with varying levels of detail.  Sometimes this feedback was so clearly about winning that it may have been difficult for individual coaching points to stick. It was pelasing to see a variety of coaching types at the club - it was just younger male coaches but a variety in age and styles.  There were also times when coaches would work together to deliver key points - this was refreshing and a pleasing outcome for all teams.

There are some positives within the interactions of coaches during game day. There is often a clear focus in relation to training outcomes. However there is great inconsistencies with overall match day communications. Greater emphasis on the need to use visuals especially for half time talks is needed, with reduced explicit information from the sidelines. More interaction especially with the number of coaches available (1-2 assistant coaches for some teams) in-game and at half-time can improve overall player development outcomes.

Generally preparation for the game is done appropriately.  Greater education and guidance for coaches in this area will allow for more effective player development on match day.

Generally speaking the coaches’ appearance, punctuality and overall conduct align with the club’s values and beliefs. Half time interactions are positive, but coaches lack consistent use of viusal aids (whiteboards). The end of the game summary often outcome focused.
I have been quite harsh here criteria 3&7 haven't been fully met by all of the coaches hence the reason I have marked them as NO

This is now John's second year in the Technical Director role. Ipswich Knights use their own portal for their player self-evaluations. For 2027 beyond making it a priority for players to have regular reviews, which leads into other forms of formal evaluation from coaches/technical staff, another consideration would be on how they will be able to have players access video clips that they are able to reflect on, and then provide their perspectives/feedback to the technical staff.

Caboolture have provided access and evidence through XPS of a good Player Self-evaluation loop. This then influences the IDPs which are developed with this input. Virginia have provided XPS access and data to support their players self-evaluation process, as well as how the process informs decisions around their IDP's and the formal evaluations that are led by coaches throughout the year. Grange have provided a basic template of a term-by-term self-evaluation for players to fill out.
