The club has only submitted two documents. One is a mid-season self-review coach check-in, which offers only surface-level reflection, and the other is a goal-setting template that is identified as a key document forming part of the club's coach IPD process.

Overall, the evidence provided is very shallow for a Prominent Gold Club and does not demonstrate that this is an embedded process within the club. Unless there is documentation in another folder or online that I am missing, there is insufficient evidence to show a comprehensive and ongoing coach reflection.

IThe club has provided an overview document in SharePoint, with additional evidence available in XPS, including a coach review completed in May that contains only superficial detail, a coach assessment score provided by Xventure without any supporting information explaining what the score relates to or how it was determined, and a template example of the assessment process. Additionally, both processes have only been completed by approximately 70% of coaches. Overall, the evidence provided is limited and does not demonstrate a comprehensive, well-established, and embedded coach development process consistent with the expectations of a Prominent Gold Club.

A good delivery submission with multiple training and match-day reflections across all coaches. While no linked videos have been uploaded, there is sufficient information provided to satisfy all other criteria

The club has a good platform to collect and track this information. However, there is no evidence of team talks being recorded, and the platform indicates that this is a single-time process rather than one that incorporates multiple reflection points throughout the season. There are good links between the information collected and individual coach development plans (IPDs), but the evidence does not fully demonstrate an ongoing reflective practice across the season.

The documents provided by the club relate to self-evaluation linked to the development of a coach IPD at the start of the season, rather than evidence demonstrating how coaches or the TD/TL have completed in-season reflection to monitor and track development areas, unless I am missing additional information. There are no links to video reviews or documentation showing that self-reflection is undertaken as a quarterly process. While the document submitted does demonstrate some reflective practice, the evidence provided does not clearly show an ongoing and structured approach to in-season coach development and review.

The club's submitted evidence in SharePoint relates primarily to self-reflection linked to the development of a coach IPD. This information is also loaded into XPS, along with a small number of Term 1 self-reviews. However, there are no links to video reviews or team talk reflections that demonstrate an embedded process throughout the club's season. Overall, there is very little evidence of ongoing reflective practice or continuous coach development..

The club has submitted evidence demonstrating that it has completed an early-season self-evaluation process and has filmed a number of team talks, meetings, and match-day activities to allow coaches to reflect on their delivery. However, there is no evidence showing how this reflection has taken place or been documented, which is why Criterion 3 has been marked as No. Based on the video evidence provided, I am satisfied that Criterion 6 can be marked as achieved, as there is evidence of TD/TL involvement in the process.

The club's SharePoint submission includes documents with a self-review section designed to support the development of an IPD. However, based on the dates provided, these appear to have been completed mid-year, around the same time as the TD/TL evaluation, rather than as part of an ongoing process. There are no filmed videos provided to support Criterion 2, and no evidence demonstrating that this is an embedded quarterly practice. Unless there is additional information available in XPS, the evidence submitted does not sufficiently demonstrate an ongoing reflective process. There is also no relevant logging detail available through the club login documentation.

A good self-review framework has been provided; however, there are no videos submitted to support Criterion 2. Additionally, the documentation suggests that self-reflections have only been completed twice during the season, rather than on a quarterly basis as required to score for creteria 4.

The club has only provided an overview delivery document that outlines the process, includes a delivery summary, and contains three filmed videos. However, I do not feel this is sufficient evidence to demonstrate that this is an embedded, club-wide process. The other document submitted is a mid-year coach reflection, which I consider to be fairly superficial and lacking in detail. It is not linked to a clear coaching framework, coaching competencies, or the coach's IPD specifically, and instead consists of only three basic reflection questions. Benefit of the doubt, that the TD/TL uses this information in the coach evaluation process for criterion 6. Dont think a score above a 2 can be awarded.

It is clear that self-analysis is being used within the club, with videos of halftime team talks, reflective activities, and training session reviews provided as evidence. However, these activities appear to have occurred only a couple of times during the season rather than on a quarterly basis. There is also no evidence demonstrating how these reflections are incorporated into TD/TL reviews and feedback processes. On balance, a score of 2 is a fair assessment for the club.

I have checked every Head Coach submission using the method outlined in the club overview document. Only two coaches have submitted evidence, and neither submission demonstrates meaningful coach development self-reflection. The content provided is largely superficial and lacks any clear reflection on coaching practice or development areas. Based on the information available in XPS, I do not believe the club has an established self-reflection process in place. Unless they have other documents or evidence that I have overlooked?

Overall, this is a good submission and provides evidence that self-review is embedded within the club throughout the season. The only query relates to the video evidence, as only three coaches have completed training video self-reflections. While this demonstrates that the process is being used, there is not enough evidence to suggest that it is fully embedded across the coaching group.

The club's submission consists of four documents: a coach self-evaluation process overview and three evaluation matrix. While the club appears to have a system for self-review, it has not presented enough evidence to confirm that this is an embedded process being consistently undertaken by all coaches. There is no information relating to video-based reflection, nor any evidence to demonstrate that the process occurs on a quarterly basis. As the criterion is linked to whether self-reflection is an embedded club-wide process, I do not believe the club can be awarded a score for Criterion 6 based on the evidence provided

This was identified as a club action plan area for this year; however, the TD chose to focus on player IPDs instead. While there is a self-review process linked to the coach IPD, the submission does not include any information or evidence relating to filmed team talks, match reviews, or similar reflective practices. There are submissions within the XPS portal, but these are inconsistent across the coaching staff in terms of both coach participation and frequency throughout the season. As a result, the evidence does not demonstrate a consistently embedded club-wide process.

The club has a process for individual self-review; however, this does not appear to occur on a quarterly basis, and there is no evidence submitted to demonstrate the use of video reflection. The self-review process does link to the club's IPD framework and is connected to the TD/TL feedback process. However, the online coach development portal does not contain information specifically related to self-reflection. Instead, the evidence provided relates primarily to formal coach reports and mentoring, with much of the information having been written by an external source rather than the individual coach. As a result, the submission does not provide sufficient evidence of an embedded self-reflection process led by coaches themselves regulary.

The club has a strong IPD process in which self-reflection is embedded. However, some of the submitted evidence appears to be TD/TL-led feedback rather than genuine self-review, as it consists of direct feedback provided to the coach rather than reflection completed by the coach themselves. While some video links have been provided, I do not believe the frequency of these activities is sufficient for the club to meet the requirements of Criterion 2.

An embedded self-reflection process is in place through XPS and is being utilised by the club. However, some of the reflection questions appear to focus more on team and match-day performance rather than the coach's own delivery and development. A good number of team talk videos have been uploaded, but it would be beneficial to see accompanying self-reflection documents completed by coaches when reviewing this footage. Additionally, I do not believe there is a clear link demonstrating how the feedback and reflections are being used to inform and support the coach's IPD process.

There is a self-reflection process in place; however, I do not see enough evidence to demonstrate that it occurs on a quarterly basis. There are no video reflections linked to match-day activities or training sessions, and most of the self-analysis submitted is connected to coach IPDs, many of which have been reviewed by the TD. While this shows some level of reflective practice, the evidence does not clearly demonstrate an ongoing, coach-led self-reflection process throughout the season.

Hard to score without access to the club's XPS account to confirm evidence of the process in action. As such, I do not believe the club can score higher than a 1, as it has documented its process but has not provided sufficient evidence to demonstrate its implementation. I would be happy to review this assessment if access to the XPS account is provided.

It's clear that the club has a process in place; however, when I review the items under each coach profile in XPS, I do not see the same level of evidence outlined in the overview submission document. Based on the information available in XPS, the only item that appears to be completed consistently across the coaching staffs 'Goal Mentoring Report'. While most coaches have documented goals, the majority have little or no data recorded against the other criteria. From what I can see, there is insufficient evidence to demonstrate that the full process is being consistently. Happy to reconsider if I have missed information in XPS.

A partial process is outlined through a number of online forms, with one linked to goal setting (completed by eight coaches) and two others related to match-day reflection, each containing only a handful of submissions. However, there is not enough evidence to confirm that a structured self-review process is embedded within the club, linked to video reflection, and actively integrated into the coach IPD process.

A good process is in place to use self-reflection to generate coach IPDs. Most coaches have completed three review periods, with the fourth expected to occur at the end of the season. However, there is no evidence that video review of match-day activities or training sessions has been used as part of the self-review process.

Hard to assess without access to XPS to confirm the monthly coach reflection submissions and the level of detail they contain. There is evidence of halftime team talks being self-reviewed, but no evidence of training session reflections. The information provided for halftime reviews is superficial and lacks sufficient detail. There is also no indication within the current submission of how these reflections link to coach IPDs or how the feedback is used within the TD/TL review process. I would be happy to review this assessment if access to XPS is granted.

The club has a basic self-reflection practice embedded within its IPD process, utilising the FQ template available in the Knowledge Base. However, self-reviews do not appear to be conducted regularly and seem to occur only at the commencement of the IPD process. There is also no evident link to ongoing video-based self-reviews connected to training sessions or match-day activities.

The club submission consists only of a self-review template and a Google Drive folder containing five team talk videos and five training videos. There is no evidence to show that coaches have completed any self-assessments throughout the course of the season. Therefore, they cannot score higher than a 1.

The club has a weekly reflection mode via google forms that guides match day and training delivery, with regular submissions throughout the season from multiple coaches. There is no information outlining how this is linked to video reviews or how it connects to the IPD process.

The club has a clear process, with greater depth of reflection evident mid-season than in pre-season following the change of Technical Director. The IPD documents demonstrate strong self-reflection, while the Coach Eye analysis is a powerful reflection tool that can be further linked to the IPD process. There is good evidence of combining self-reflection with mentoring feedback within the IPDs. Self are dodument 3 timesime per season, as per oveview doudment.

The club's submission only consists of a template form and an update of matchday photos and videos. The club has not submitted any documents that provide evidence that its coaches have completed any self-assessment reviews throughout the season. The document in the folder that provides an outline of what they do does not provide any evidence of self-assessment activity. The club's score could possibly be a zero for this line item.
Only two template documents were submitted. There is no evidence of any self-reflection process embedded within the club submitted.

A good self-review process is linked to the development of a coach IPD, including goal setting and identified development areas. While an ongoing reflection journal is documented within the IPD and a quarterly review is scheduled, I do not believe there is sufficient detail to score highly against these two criteria. I would expect to see more detailed evidence demonstrating how self-reflection is documented and reviewed in greater depth. Currently, it appears to be more of a high-level, tick-box exercise rather than a comprehensive reflection process.

While match day and training information is included within the IPD document, there is no evidence of a match day or training video self-reflection process being implemented.

Only a small group of coaches have completed self-reviews, and even those that have are limited to surface-level detail and information that is not directly related to the self-reflection process within the IPD. There is no evidence of match day or training video self-reviews being conducted. While each coach has an IPD, the documents do not clearly outline a structured coach self-review process. Overall, the IPDs appear to be high-level documents with limited depth. There is also no evidence that this is an ongoing quarterly process throughout the season.

The coach observation feedback has a spelling mistake in 'proficient'. The template for the observation feedback should have a date to allow for reference. The feedback form allows formal feedback provided for specific sessions, this could be done for all coaches, as all coaches have an area to focus on session delivery within their Coach IDP (understand coaches can choose what support they want as well). Furthermore, only 1 was done for each coach, while the focused development schedule has 2 training observations within its plan.

For more effective development of coaches, it is recommended to increase the frequency of touch point to allow Phase 2 to be completed (none completed), and perhaps a 2nd cycle of IDPs. Similar to the Observation Feedback Form, there should be a date linked to Phase 1 and Phase 2 as it seems like it occurs across a period of time. 

Additionally, greater detail in terms of feedback from the Coach Developer within the coach IDP will help with formal feedback (criteria 4 not met). E.g. additional column for mentor to complete for Phase 1 on how they will support the goal, or include coverage of match days, the template is quite brief.

The IDP template allows for significant input from the coach, however there is little for the coach mentor/developer to contribute. Additionally there is no evidenced check-in thorughout the season, having only 1 at the end of the season is not great, especially when there are some reviews that were mentioned should occur every term, etc. (criteria 4 not met). Looking into the coaches' IDPs in detail, there are a few coaches who may have inappropriate goals in relation to the players' ages/stages that are working with (e.g. result focused goals or opposition analysis) - it is important to ensure these are aligned as per the clubs P2 document. 

The 4 pillars that coaches are encouraged to build their IDP around is a good idea but may not occur in reality. It might be good to have that within the template and coaches to choose at least 2 or 3 of 4 categories to diversify their goals.

Overall template is great, with comprehensive plan in coach education / career goals, as well as an 'easy on the eye' scoring system. It is recommended to extend the review items to include personal competencies such as organisation, communication, leadership, culture, etc. as the current lists are all football related competencies. (criteria 2 not met). 

Additionally, only review 1 is completed, with a planned follow up mid-season not met (criteria 5 is not met).

There is ongoing mentor network at the club (criteria 7 is met).

The club has its own platform in which there are individual coach profiles and relevant self-evaluation input, there is no clear coach IDP that involves both the coach and TD/TL/mentor input. There is no evidence on when these are done, and when the mid-season check ins are (if any).

Coaches may need more guidance on their focus areas as a couple of junior coaches have tactical areas as their areas of support, and some have result-related objectives which may not be appropriate to the age/stages that they are coaching (criteria 3 not met)

The overall template of the IDPs are great, particularly the bit on super strengths and development areas which cover the areas of coaching the club believes supports its methodology. Despite having a template for each coach, there are some that are not completed (hence criteria 4 is not met). Additionally, it is unclear when the check in points throughout the season are, with no info on the weekly self assessments tracking by any coach (criteria 5 and 8 not met). There is also little suggestion within the template on personal and professional growth (criteria 6 not met). 

D24 submission states the mentor for each coach (criteria 7 met).

IDP of coaches provided are only a one-off document, which differs from the information provided on the powerpoint slide that included an overview of the season summary. It includes an end of season review (criteria 8 ticked off in good faith). This is a key area to improve delivery wise as the planning aspect is great.

There is a lack of comprehensive list of competencies to include football and personal competencies with general comments on strengths and developmental areas. There is a list of mentoring provided by Technical Directors/Leads and Senior coache at the club (as per D24 powerpoint doc.).

There is great amount of evidence that the club has delivered in this line item with goal setting, self assessment, coach reviews and season reviews - check-ins are done for each term. There is use of video as a tool for self-reflection and feedback, which is a strong point of differentiation from other clubs. The line management division is great to allow clear roles from TD/TLs and consistent touch points, however the challenge is to ensure that the quality of feedback and IDPs across different line managements are similar and of a high quality - there are some inconsistencies observed. 

Overall done well, but it is recommended to ensure all documents are clearly dated and potentially migrated to online documents to allow ease of long-term storage (especially if the club's aim is to keep coaches for the long haul).

There are IDPs provided for each coach which include self coach competency frameworks and mid year coach development reviews but these are not dated, with the open ended questions of most coaches completed in July and August (criteria 5 not met). There are areas within the coaches IDP that include non football competencies such as the learning environment and professional behaviours.

Greater amount of detail should be included within the IDP templates such as the 'How' to bridge the identified areas for improvements. Also, it can include goal settings over the longer term, and include assigned mentors.

The IDP template is basic with no dates for the coaching assessment marking components or the DISC scores - it is recommended to add dates for tracking and evidence purposes. The different aspects of the coach assessment are comprehensive - including both football and personal competencies. There are inconsistencies with completion of the goal setting components. 

To improve on the IDP template, the club should look to expand and include the 'How' in the form of an action plan to support the development plans.

SWOT analysis and the goal setting template is a good starting point, however there is no evidence of any check-in point. There is no template of the list of competencies that guides coaches with the goal setting - it is recommended to have a list of football and personal competencies in relation to the club's preferred coaching methodology and coach profile (P2). There is also no evidence of what a season ending performance review looks like. There is a named mentor within the coach IDP but there is little evidence there is specific additional support individualised to the coach.

There is a well documented CDP with goals setting, strengths and areas of improvement input from both coach and TD with feedback. There is a review each term (2-3 done for most coaches) with a last one at the end of the season. It is recommended to have a date for each review throughout the year for documentation purposes, and also an area for the mentor/TD/TL to input for feedback. 

There is little info on benchmarks provided for coaches on personal and professional growth with no info on the coaches pathway within or outside the club.

The overall IDP template is simple with good amount of feedback provided by the TD/TL on different personal and football competencies. However it seems like a one-off with little info on follow ups during the season or a review at the end. 

It would be recommended to increase the touch points throughout the year, but also add in components in relation to a self reflection or goal setting at the start of the season, where coaches can have their input within their own IDPs.

Great document that has specific criteria that is linked to the club's 'The Mitchie Way' and key coaching behaviours with clear dates throughout for documentation and evidence purposes - this is worthy to be used as short shared best practice. The whole document provides evidence in planning for multiple check points throughout the season, including a comprehensive season ending performance review - it is noted however most coaches do not have their review section completed but criteria is ticked off with what I observed at club training. It is essential this is delivered and documented fully for 2027.

The format of the CDP and evidence is poor and hard to understand. There is some thought in the planning to ensure multiple touch points throughout the season which seems to have occurred through some bits of the season, however there is no season review at the end. The level of detail overall is poor with no clear strength and areas of improvement documentation. Additionally, there is no clear list of football and personal competencies provided to coaches as a guide (or something that is unique to Brisbane Strikers).

Overall the recommendation is to improve on the clarity and consistency of the documentation, and to increase the level of input from the coaches and overall level of detail from the TL/TD.

The PPT template for coach DAP is done well, with coverage on the 4 pillars of the Coach Competency Framework (with both coach and mentor input), session observation, feedback, and action plan (and includes dates) however most of these are not completed. The XPS info for the junior coaches are mostly completed in the last month or so (July), and has no input from the coach. 

Mentor network iprimarily nvolves the Technical Leads at the club.

Complementing the 2, and ensuring prompt delivery of the components (regular touch points throughout the season) will elevate the Coach IDP process at the club.

Overall there is a clear process in how coaches are developed via the use of a comprehensive IDP on the portal. It includes goal setting, feedback from TD Matthew on training and match days, as well as great detail info on both football and personal competencies. The portal allows evidence to be logged and this was done consistently across coaches.

To increase effectiveness of coach development, it may be beneficial to explore other input for coach development, instead of only the TD running the overarching process. E.g. pairing coaches of a certain strength with areas of improvement, external mentor, etc.

The planning of the overall delivering of coach development and review schedule is great with some good information but there is little evidence (via dated documents) that reflect the consistent touch points as mentioned. 

The IDP template itself is simple and can be expanded to increase the level of detail to include goal setting (incl longer career outlook), increase coverage of personal competencies, coach input, etc. It is recommended to include dates and mentors within templates and ensure the execution of the reviews is as consistent as per the planning.

The input and set up on XPS is done quite well (dated with initials of mentor for each input), with the supporting and mentoring timeline well documented on the P14 document. However the confusion and inconsistency appears with timelines of when the different checkpoints should occur - the challenge going into 2027 is to ensure the coaches, TLs and TD adhere to the timeline that is set out. 

It is recommended to include longer term goal setting and also clear benchmarks and paths within and outside the club.

The process outlined within the powerpoint is robust however with the TD taking sole responsibility in delivering all aspects, it can be too onerous. This is reflected on the Coach IDPs provided which all seemed to be completed in July. 

With the TD also only joining the club in mid March, it is expected that there is an improvement in the consistency of delivery and planning for the 2027 season. It is recommended to have some area with coaches' input to include goal setting(including mid-long term plans) and their self reflection based on the IDP templates so that it is a collaborative approach in creating the coach IDPs.

Within the folders only documents related to 5 coaches are uploaded, with inconsistency with the documents for each coach (criteria 1 not met). The documents are also not dated and seem to occur only once off during the season. (criteria 5 and 8 not met). The template can be improved to be more user friendly and easy on the eyes. The content is holistic, including professional, interpersonal and intrapersonal knowledge - well done. For the completed documents, the feedback provided by the TD is at a high level. 

Overall, there are huge inconsistencies within the delivery of the IDPs, with no evidence for more than half the coaches at the club, as a result I cannot justify a score higher than a 1.

There is clear evidence based on the Coach Development Plan tab on XPS that there are regular check-ins and it is assumed that a season ending review will be held in the coming month. There are personal competencies included within the coaching principles tab which seems to be completed once off. The detail within the CDP is brief and it is recommended to include the different aspects of football competencies within the coach methodology at the club as a guide (similar to the definitions within the Coaching Principles tab).

The IDP template and detail provided for coaches is very basic. There is only 1 entry per coach with no date on the IDP.  Of note the word and PDF action plans cannot be accessed for some reason.

This is a major area to focus on for 2027. It is recommended to have a clear plan in touch points throughout the season, and improve the template to allow coaches input when working with a mentor for a collaborative creation of IDPs, including in-depth action plans (what kind of support is provided?) for coaches.

There is clear consistent review for all the coaches with the evidence provided, the assumption that there will be a season ending review in the next month or so. The level of detail is average and can be improved to increase the quality of feedback the coaches receive. The process seems to only involve the TD, it is encouraged to expand the input to include that of the coach (more collaborative) and also the Technical Leads at the club.

There is a fair amount of documents that supports coach development at the club, however the naming convention are confusing and should be improved upon for the 2027 submission for greater overall clarity. Understand there is a transition to XPS - this is an area to improve to ensure alignment and clarity between coaches and TD/TLs. The overall depth of detail is missing, although there is good coverage of football and personal competencies. The weekly monitoring log is a good way to track informal touchpoints however it seems to be completed only in the first few months of 2026 - this may be because the process is carried mostly by the TD Dave (unsure due to lack of initials of the person logging the interaction). Benefit of the doubt provided regarding a season ending review that will be held in the next month or so.

The IDP template is basic - it provides input from coaches on football and personal competencies but there is limited/no input from the TLs/TD. There is also no regular touch points throughout the season. It is suggested for the club to focus improvement in this area for 2027.

IDP templates provided for all Academy coaches. The completion of the IDPs are poor, with most IDPs incomplete. Only the youth boys coaches have formal feedback documented (criteria 4 not met). 

There is only 1 IDP document per coach, with no evidence of regular check-in points to track progress (criteria 5 not met). There is also little evidence on benchmarks for personal and professional growth with no mentor network evidenced. 

Overall this line item is delivered poorly and is a key area to focus on for 2027.

The templates and examples of Coach Development Plans are rather comprehensive with good detail. The objectivity of the Competency Evaluation is a point of differentiation from other clubs. It is important to ensure for 2027 that ALL coaches' CDPs are uploaded with clear check in points documented throughout the season. 

A fair bit of the evidence are irrelevant for the D23 Coach IDP line item and are more related to D22 Self Evaluation, D24 Coach Mentoring and D25 Education Events.

The IDP template despite being simple contains a good amount of information to provide key insights into a coach's strength, areas of improvements and methods of support. It is also designed to be completed collaboratively between the coach and allocated mentor. 

Overall simple but done really well, an item that can be used as shared best practice.

The submission overall is very messy and needs to be rectified for 2027. The club has a form that is named CPD review form - which is not the actual IDP document. There is some mention on professional development (coaches wanting to complete advanced courses - however it is recommended to have a more holistic coverage to include both football and personal competencies within its IDP template and review. 

The CDP review form involves 3 touchpoints across the season, meeting criteria 5. Overall this is an area that the club needs guidance on, if they are unable to organise effectively between the technical leadership within the club.

The list of coaches with IDPs are only from the boys program, with no evidence of a coach within the girls program having one (criteria 1 not met). The detail within the IDP is superfical at times and general.

It is unsure with the 1 document and no dates within different sections of the IDP that there are multiple check in points (minimum once per term) that occurs, however benefit of doubt is given that an end season review will be held (criteria 5 not met but 8 is).

There is a brief section on the possible pathway within the club within the Coach Develop Strategy PDF - this should be expanded to include greater detail on the benchmark for coaches to qualify to move on within the pathway (criteria 6 not met). Overall the template needs be improved to include dates (and regular updates) and sections for coaches to have some input to allow for greater collaboration from the coaches to create their own IDPs

The overall template of the coach's IDP is very holistic, with guidance included within the document and overall good depth of detail provided in the feedback. Additionally, it would be beneficial to improve on the template to include dates on when it is revisited and when goals are ticked off or renewed with more action plans during the in-season reviews.

Overall this is a key area to focus on improving for 2027.
